content.text: The "namespace group" concept is in `namespaceRouting` (`refs/heads/entire/native/*` for GitHub groups). I'll read the repolookup proto contract.

content.content:
1	// RepoLookup is the internal cross-jurisdictional directory: given upstream
2	// mirror coordinates, returns every (jurisdiction, cluster_slug) that
3	// mirrors them. Used by webhook ingest to fan a single upstream event out
4	// across the per-cluster NATS subjects defined by ADR 20260408.
5	//
6	// Auth: mTLS-only. The receiver listener gates by per-listener workload
7	// allowlist (ADR 20260501); there is no end-user identity in these calls.
8	
9	syntax = "proto3";
10	
11	package repolookup.v1;
12	
13	option go_package = "entire.io/gen/proto/internalapi/repolookup/v1;repolookupv1";
14	
15	service RepoLookup {
16	  // LookupByMirror resolves upstream mirror coordinates to every routable
17	  // placement that hosts a mirror of them. An upstream may be mirrored in
18	  // multiple jurisdictions/clusters; the response carries the full list,
19	  // ordered by (jurisdiction, cluster_slug).
20	  //
21	  // Placements without a cluster_slug (legacy rows still in the COR-138
22	  // backfill window) are filtered server-side and logged at warn level —
23	  // they are not addressable on per-cluster NATS subjects, so returning
24	  // them would silently route work nowhere. An empty response means no
25	  // routable mirror exists; it does not distinguish "no mirror at all"
26	  // from "all mirrors are still unstamped."
27	  rpc LookupByMirror(LookupByMirrorRequest) returns (LookupByMirrorResponse);
28	
29	  // LookupMirrorByID is LookupByMirror's inverse: given a mirror's EntireDB
30	  // repo ULID, return the upstream coordinates (provider/owner/repo) it
31	  // mirrors. Callers that hold only the mirror_repos id — e.g. a consumer of a
32	  // resource_lifecycle_v1 mirror.created event, whose payload is a thin
33	  // resource_id-only projection — use it to recover the (owner, repo) they
34	  // need to act on the mirror (COR-717: seed github_repo_meta on mirror
35	  // creation). Returns CodeNotFound when no mirror_repos row matches the id (or
36	  // the placement is suspended); CodeInvalidArgument when repo_id is empty or
37	  // not a valid ULID.
38	  rpc LookupMirrorByID(LookupMirrorByIDRequest) returns (LookupMirrorByIDResponse);
39	
40	  // LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID resolves a repo id (any placement of a native
41	  // repo — primary or native mirror; the id a repo_refs_v1 ref event carries) to
42	  // its group's git-data HOME placement and every REPLICATION-eligible
43	  // native-mirror placement (ADR 20260720-native-mirroring). Replica fan-out
44	  // consumes this: it drops the event unless its local cluster is the home
45	  // (loop prevention), then publishes one sync job per native mirror.
46	  // source_url is the home cluster's INTERNAL by-ID git URL, computed here so
47	  // fanout and the worker stay source-agnostic; it is never user-facing.
48	  //
49	  // Native mirrors below the serving stage (still being created), suspended, or
50	  // marked for deletion are excluded. Placements that ARE listed may still hold
51	  // an empty or partially-synced repo — a placement is listed from the moment
52	  // it is registered, and that replication traffic is what makes it converge,
53	  // so this response is not a statement that a mirror can serve READS. Read
54	  // routing gates separately, on the placement having converged; do not reuse
55	  // this RPC to answer "where may I read this repo from". An ungrouped repo
56	  // resolves to home = its own placement with no mirrors of either kind. A
57	  // GitHub mirror group resolves the same way unless one of its placements
58	  // owns the group's git data, in which case home is that owner and the
59	  // siblings come back as namespace_mirrors (see below); full-repo GitHub
60	  // mirroring still routes through LookupByMirror, not here. CodeNotFound
61	  // when the repo id is unknown; CodeInvalidArgument when it is empty or not
62	  // a ULID.
63	  rpc LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID(LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDRequest) returns (LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDResponse);
64	}
65	
66	message LookupByMirrorRequest {
67	  // Upstream provider, e.g. "github". Required.
68	  string provider = 1;
69	
70	  // Upstream owner segment (org or user), e.g. "octocat". Required.
71	  string owner = 2;
72	
73	  // Upstream repo name, e.g. "hello-world". Required.
74	  string repo = 3;
75	
76	  // GitHub's immutable numeric repo id, from the webhook's repository.id.
77	  // Optional; 0 means unknown. When set, only placements of that upstream are
78	  // returned: owner/repo can be stale on our side (a teardown leaked, then the
79	  // owner renamed away) and claimed by another GitHub account, whose events
80	  // must not route onto the old mirror (ENT-2822).
81	  int64 github_repo_id = 4;
82	}
83	
84	message LookupByMirrorResponse {
85	  repeated Placement placements = 1;
86	}
87	
88	message LookupMirrorByIDRequest {
89	  // Crockford Base32 ULID of the mirrored repo within EntireDB. Required.
90	  string repo_id = 1;
91	}
92	
93	message LookupMirrorByIDResponse {
94	  // Upstream provider, e.g. "github". Always "github" today — mirror_repos
95	  // joins github_repos for its upstream coordinates.
96	  string provider = 1;
97	
98	  // Upstream owner segment (org or user), e.g. "octocat".
99	  string owner = 2;
100	
101	  // Upstream repo name, e.g. "hello-world".
102	  string repo = 3;
103	}
104	
105	message Placement {
106	  // Crockford Base32 ULID of the mirrored repo within EntireDB.
107	  string repo_id = 1;
108	
109	  // Jurisdiction that homes this mirror, e.g. "us" / "eu".
110	  string jurisdiction = 2;
111	
112	  // Cluster slug within the jurisdiction that homes this mirror, e.g.
113	  // "royalcanin". Guaranteed non-empty: rows whose repo_registry row has
114	  // not yet been cluster-stamped are filtered out by the server before
115	  // the response is built (see service comment on LookupByMirror).
116	  string cluster_slug = 3;
117	}
118	
119	message LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDRequest {
120	  // Crockford Base32 ULID of any placement of the repo. Required.
121	  string repo_id = 1;
122	}
123	
124	message LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDResponse {
125	  // The group's git-data home placement — where pushes land.
126	  Placement home = 1;
127	
128	  // Replication-eligible native-mirror placements, ordered by (jurisdiction,
129	  // cluster_slug). Empty for repos with no native mirrors (every repo
130	  // today). Listed placements are sync TARGETS, not necessarily readable
131	  // sources — see the RPC comment.
132	  repeated Placement native_mirrors = 2;
133	
134	  // The home cluster's INTERNAL by-ID git URL for the primary
135	  // (https://<internal host>/git/repo/<primary ULID>) — the sync job's
136	  // fetch source. Empty when the home cluster has no internal URL
137	  // registered. Never user-facing.
138	  string source_url = 3;
139	
140	  // Namespace-mirror placements: the other ready placements of a GitHub
141	  // group whose git data is owned by one of them (COR-1566). They receive
142	  // entiredb_ns sync jobs, which replicate ONLY the Entire-owned
143	  // refs/heads/entire/native/* namespace from source_url — the rest of
144	  // their ref state comes from GitHub. Ordered by (jurisdiction,
145	  // cluster_slug); empty for every group without an owner, and never
146	  // populated together with native_mirrors (a group is one kind or the
147	  // other).
148	  repeated Placement namespace_mirrors = 4;
149	}

15		"github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/internal/mirrorjobs"

17		"github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/pkg/refevents"
18	)

20	// Native-mirror trigger consumer (COR-1021): consumes the LOCAL cluster's
21	// repo_refs_v1 ref-event stream and publishes one mirror.git sync_repo job per
22	// serving native mirror of the pushed repo — the event-driven fast path that
23	// keeps native mirrors fresh. Enabled per cluster via
24	// FANOUT_NATIVE_MIRROR_CONSUMER_ENABLED; a no-op while no native mirrors exist
25	// (every event resolves to an empty route set and Acks).
26	const (
27		// nativeMirrorDurable is the pull-consumer durable on repo_refs_v1. A fixed
28		// name (unlike FANOUT_DURABLE) is safe here because the stream itself is
29		// per-cluster local — durables are stream-scoped, so two clusters' consumers
30		// can never collide on one stream the way the shared US webhook stream's
31		// could.
32		nativeMirrorDurable = "native-mirror-fanout"
33	
34		// Retry envelope: same flat-NakWithDelay shape as the webhook consumer.
35		// repo_refs_v1 is limits-retention, so an exhausted delivery is simply not
36		// redelivered again (nothing orphans, nothing pins). A dropped event is
37		// healed by the primary's next push — every sync replicates full ref
38		// state — so no DLQ is wired (rev 11: v1 accepts "next push" as the
39		// staleness RPO). No InactiveThreshold either: an abandoned durable on a
40		// limits stream pins nothing.
41		nativeMirrorFailureDelay = 30 * time.Second
42		nativeMirrorMaxDeliver   = 8
43		nativeMirrorAckWait      = 30 * time.Second
44	)
45	
46	// Ack reasons for benign no-op dispositions, recorded on the completed metric
47	// so drops are observable without per-event logs (not_home fires on every
48	// worker-push echo in a mirror cluster; no_native_mirrors on every push in a
49	// home cluster — both far too hot to log).
50	const (
51		ackReasonTlogRef      = "tlog_ref"          // transparency-log ref churn; the branch event triggers the sync
52		ackReasonRepoNotFound = "repo_not_found"    // repo deleted between event publish and consume
53		ackReasonNotHome      = "not_home"          // event echoed from a native-mirror placement (loop prevention)
54		ackReasonNoMirrors    = "no_native_mirrors" // repo has no serving native mirrors (every repo today)
55	
56		// ackReasonNamespaceOutOfScope fires on a namespace group (a GitHub
57		// group whose git data one placement owns): those placements replicate
58		// only the Entire-owned namespace from here, so every other ref —
59		// refs/heads/main, tags, HEAD symref moves — is acked without a job.
60		// Hot on the owner cell: one per ordinary push.
61		ackReasonNamespaceOutOfScope = "namespace_out_of_scope"
62	)
63	
64	// namespaceRefPrefix is the Entire-owned branch namespace replicated by
65	// entiredb_ns jobs (COR-1566). The worker enforces the same scope on the
66	// sync itself; this filter only keeps the jobs off the stream.
67	const namespaceRefPrefix = "refs/heads/entire/native/"
68	
69	// newNativeMirrorConsumer wires the ref-event resolver into the shared
70	// fanoutengine runtime. Same worker pool knobs and region map as the webhook
71	// consumer; no DLQ (see the retry-envelope comment above).
72	func newNativeMirrorConsumer(js nats.JetStreamContext, resolver *nativeMirrorSyncResolver, regions fanoutengine.Regions, metrics *fanoutMetrics, concurrency, fetchBatch int) *fanoutengine.Consumer {
73		return fanoutengine.New(js, refEventDecoder{}, resolver, regions, hooksFor(metrics), fanoutengine.Config{
74			Subject:         refevents.NATSSubjectPrefix + ">",
75			Stream:          refevents.NATSStreamName,
76			Durable:         nativeMirrorDurable,
77			Tracer:          tracerName,
78			SpanName:        "fanout.native_mirror.dispatch",
79			DestinationName: refevents.NATSStreamName,
80			AckWait:         nativeMirrorAckWait,
81			MaxDeliver:      nativeMirrorMaxDeliver,
82			NakDelay:        nativeMirrorFailureDelay,
83			SpanAttrs:       stampRefEventSpanAttrs,
84			Concurrency:     concurrency,
85			FetchBatch:      fetchBatch,
86		})
87	}
88	
89	// refEventDecoder turns a raw repo_refs_v1 delivery into the engine envelope.
90	// A decode failure → Term (bad envelope). Event carries the ref op so the
91	// completed metric's event attribute stays low-cardinality: the KNOWN wire
92	// vocabulary (create/update/delete/force_update/symref_update) passes
93	// through, anything else is clamped to "other" — Unmarshal tolerates
94	// newer-producer payloads by design, so the wire value is unbounded even
95	// though the payload is valid. DeliveryID is the producer's
96	// content+timestamp identity, which doubles as the engine's route-memo key.
97	type refEventDecoder struct{}
98	
99	// eventOther stands in for a ref op outside the known vocabulary on the
100	// metric attribute, so a future producer op can't create unbounded metric
101	// cardinality. Spans/logs still carry the real op via the resolver.
102	const eventOther = "other"
103	
104	var knownRefOps = map[string]bool{
105		refevents.RefOpCreate:       true,
106		refevents.RefOpUpdate:       true,
107		refevents.RefOpDelete:       true,
108		refevents.RefOpForceUpdate:  true,
109		refevents.RefOpSymrefUpdate: true,
110	}
111	
112	func (refEventDecoder) Decode(data []byte) (fanoutengine.Envelope, error) {
113		ev, err := refevents.Unmarshal(data)
114		if err != nil {
115			return fanoutengine.Envelope{}, err
116		}
117		event := ev.RefOp
118		if !knownRefOps[event] {
119			event = eventOther
120		}
121		return fanoutengine.Envelope{
122			Event:      event,
123			DeliveryID: ev.DeliveryID(),
124			ObservedAt: ev.Timestamp,
125			Body:       data,
126		}, nil
127	}
128	
129	// stampRefEventSpanAttrs stamps the envelope-level identity; the resolver adds
130	// the repo/ref attributes once it has re-decoded the body.
131	func stampRefEventSpanAttrs(span trace.Span, env fanoutengine.Envelope) {
132		span.SetAttributes(
133			attribute.String("entire.ref_event.op", env.Event),
134			attribute.String("entire.ref_event.delivery_id", env.DeliveryID),
135		)
136	}
137	
138	// nativeRouteResolver is the mirrorjobs.NativeMirrorResolver surface this
139	// consumer needs, narrowed for tests.
140	type nativeRouteResolver interface {
141		NativeMirrorRoutes(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (mirrorjobs.NativeMirrorResolution, error)
142	}
143	
144	// nativeMirrorSyncResolver resolves local ref events into mirror.git sync_repo
145	// routes, one per serving native mirror. It is the engine's Resolver for the
146	// native-mirror consumer.
147	//
148	// Loop prevention: a worker push into a native-mirror placement emits ref
149	// events on THAT cluster's repo_refs_v1 too. Those events resolve to a home
150	// cluster different from this consumer's local cluster and are dropped, so a
151	// sync can never trigger another sync. Only the home cluster — where user
152	// pushes land — fans out.
153	type nativeMirrorSyncResolver struct {
154		routes         nativeRouteResolver
155		localClusterID string
156	}
157	
158	func newNativeMirrorSyncResolver(routes nativeRouteResolver, localClusterID string) *nativeMirrorSyncResolver {
159		return &nativeMirrorSyncResolver{routes: routes, localClusterID: localClusterID}
160	}
161	
162	// Resolve returns one sync_repo route per serving mirror of the pushed repo.
163	// For a native-mirror group every ref op fans out — hash transitions move
164	// objects, and a symref_update (default-branch move) is reconciled by the
165	// worker's post-sync HEAD follow, the entiredb twin of the webhook path's
166	// default-branch edit. For a namespace group only refs under
167	// namespaceRefPrefix fan out; the rest of that repo's ref state belongs to
168	// GitHub's own mirroring. Transparency-log refs are skipped either way: every
169	// push writes them alongside the branch ref, so the branch event already
170	// triggers the (full-ref-state) sync.
171	func (d *nativeMirrorSyncResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context, _ string, _ string, _ time.Time, body []byte) ([]fanoutengine.Route, string, error) {
172		ev, err := refevents.Unmarshal(body)
173		if err != nil {
174			// Unreachable in practice — Decode already validated this payload —
175			// kept as an input error so a future decoder/resolver drift Terms
176			// instead of redelivering a poison payload forever.
177			return nil, "", fanoutengine.Input("invalid ref event: %v", err)
178		}
179		if ev.RepoID == "" {
180			// Unmarshal tolerates absent fields by design (independent producer
181			// deploys), but an event with no repo id can never resolve — an
182			// input error (Term), not a Nak, or the poison payload would ride
183			// all MaxDeliver redeliveries for nothing.
184			return nil, "", fanoutengine.Input("ref event has no repo_id")
185		}
186	
187		if strings.HasPrefix(ev.RefName, "refs/tlog/") {
188			return nil, ackReasonTlogRef, nil
189		}
190	
191		// Stamp the parent span with the source coordinates so dropped or failed
192		// deliveries are still findable by repo id. entire.ref_event.op is
193		// re-stamped with the WIRE value: the decoder's envelope clamps unknown
194		// ops to "other" for metric cardinality, but the span can carry the
195		// real one.
196		span := trace.SpanFromContext(ctx)
197		span.SetAttributes(
198			attribute.String("entire.source_kind", "entiredb"),
199			attribute.String("entire.repo_id", ev.RepoID),
200			attribute.String("entire.ref_name", ev.RefName),
201			attribute.String("entire.ref_event.op", ev.RefOp),
202		)
203	
204		res, err := d.routes.NativeMirrorRoutes(ctx, ev.RepoID)
205		if err != nil {
206			if errors.Is(err, mirrorjobs.ErrNativeRepoNotFound) {
207				// Repo deleted between event publish and consume: benign skip.
208				span.AddEvent("native_mirror.repo_not_found")
209				slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Ref event for unknown repo; skipping",
210					slog.String("repo_id", ev.RepoID), slog.String("ref_name", ev.RefName))
211				return nil, ackReasonRepoNotFound, nil
212			}
213			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Native mirror route resolution failed",
214				slog.String("repo_id", ev.RepoID), slog.Any("error", err))
215			return nil, "", err
216		}
217	
218		if res.HomeClusterID != d.localClusterID {
219			// Mirror-side echo of a worker push (or an event for a repo homed
220			// elsewhere): only the home cluster fans out.
221			span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("entire.native_mirror.home_cluster_id", res.HomeClusterID))
222			return nil, ackReasonNotHome, nil
223		}
224	
225		if len(res.NamespaceRoutes) > 0 && !strings.HasPrefix(ev.RefName, namespaceRefPrefix) {
226			return nil, ackReasonNamespaceOutOfScope, nil
227		}
228	
229		routes := slices.Concat(res.Routes, res.NamespaceRoutes)
230		if len(routes) == 0 {
231			return nil, ackReasonNoMirrors, nil
232		}
233	
234		out := make([]fanoutengine.Route, 0, len(routes))
235		for _, route := range routes {
236			out = append(out, gitSyncRoute{route: route})
237		}
238		return out, "", nil
239	}

1	# cmd/fanout
2	
3	Runs up to two pull consumers, selected per cluster by env flags, that turn
4	source-repo change events into mirror sync-job publishes on `mirror_git_v1`:
5	
6	- **Webhook consumer** (`FANOUT_WEBHOOK_CONSUMER_ENABLED`, default on):
7	  pull-subscribes the `webhooks_github_v1` stream and fans each GitHub
8	  `push` webhook out into one sync job per mirror placement. US-only — the
9	  webhook stream exists only where GitHub ingress lands.
10	- **Native-mirror consumer** (`FANOUT_NATIVE_MIRROR_CONSUMER_ENABLED`,
11	  default off; COR-1021): pull-subscribes the LOCAL cluster's
12	  `repo_refs_v1` ref-event stream and fans each home-cluster ref change out
13	  into one sync job per serving native mirror. Per-cluster — every cluster
14	  that homes native repos runs it.
15	
16	GitHub installation/repo metadata is **not** fanout's job: entire-core-global
17	consumes `webhooks_github_v1` directly for that (COR-523). fanout used to also
18	emit perms jobs onto `mirror_perms_v1`; that path has been removed.
19	
20	## Topology
21	
22	```
23	webhooks_github_v1 ──(pull, durable=$FANOUT_DURABLE)───────▶  cmd/fanout
24	repo_refs_v1       ──(pull, durable=native-mirror-fanout)──▶    │
25	                                                                ├──▶ Core.LookupByMirror /
26	                                                                │    Core.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID (mTLS)
27	                                                                └──▶ mirror_git_v1  (sync_repo jobs,
28	                                                                     routed to each placement's NATS)
29	```
30	
31	The other `webhooks_github_v1` consumers (`cmd/meta-fanout`,
32	`cmd/core-fanout`, `cmd/trails-fanout`) are independent durables on the same
33	upstream webhook stream — each sees every message via its own ack state.
34	
35	## Configuration
36	
37	| env var                                | required | default | notes |
38	| -------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ----- |
39	| `ENTIRE_NATS_URL`                      | yes      | —       | Local JetStream URL. |
40	| `ENTIRE_CORE_INTERNAL_URL`             | yes      | —       | entire-core RepoLookup mTLS listener. |
41	| `ENTIRE_INTERNAL_TLS_CERT_FILE`        | yes      | —       | Workload PCA cert (DNS SAN `fanout`). |
42	| `ENTIRE_INTERNAL_TLS_KEY_FILE`         | yes      | —       | |
43	| `ENTIRE_INTERNAL_TLS_CA_FILE`          | yes      | —       | |
44	| `FANOUT_WEBHOOK_CONSUMER_ENABLED`      | no       | `true`  | GitHub webhook consumer. Disable on clusters without the US-only `webhooks_github_v1` stream (an enabled consumer there loops on "stream not found" and holds `/readyz` false). |
45	| `FANOUT_NATIVE_MIRROR_CONSUMER_ENABLED`| no       | `false` | Native-mirror trigger consumer on the local `repo_refs_v1` stream. At least one consumer must be enabled. |
46	| `FANOUT_DURABLE`                       | yes¹     | —       | Webhook pull-consumer durable. Must be distinct per region. |
47	| `LISTEN_ADDR`                          | no       | `:8080` | |
48	| `FANOUT_LOCAL_CLUSTER_ID`              | yes²     | —       | This pod's cluster_id (matches `Placement.ClusterID`/`cluster_slug` from Core). Required when `FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS` is set, and always when the native-mirror consumer is enabled (it is the loop-prevention key). |
49	| `FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS`                  | no       | empty   | Multi-region routing: `cluster_id=url,cluster_id=url,...` for **remote** NATS clusters to dial. Empty = single-region (every publish → local). With the native-mirror consumer enabled, every overlay must carry the full remote map — an empty map silently publishes cross-cluster jobs to local NATS, where no worker consumes their subject. |
50	
51	¹ Required only when the webhook consumer is enabled.
52	² Required when `FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS` is set, or when the native-mirror
53	consumer is enabled.
54	
55	`FANOUT_DURABLE` must be distinct per region (e.g. `fanout-us-east-2`,
56	`fanout-eu-central-1`). JetStream durables are stream-scoped; sharing one
57	across regions on the same upstream stream collapses the consumers. The
58	native-mirror consumer's durable is fixed (`native-mirror-fanout`) instead:
59	its stream is per-cluster local, so no two clusters can collide.
60	
61	## Native-mirror trigger (COR-1021)
62	
63	Each cluster's entiredb publishes one `repo_refs_v1` event per committed ref
64	change on any repo it hosts. The native-mirror consumer:
65	
66	1. skips `refs/tlog/*` churn (the branch event already triggers the sync);
67	2. resolves the event's repo id through the cached
68	   `Core.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID`;
69	3. **drops the event unless this cluster is the repo group's git-data home**
70	   — loop prevention: a worker push into a native-mirror placement echoes on
71	   THAT cluster's stream, and without the home check a sync would trigger
72	   another sync;
73	4. publishes one `sync_repo` job (`SourceKindEntireDB`, `Source.URL` = the
74	   home cluster's internal by-ID git URL) per serving native mirror, routed
75	   to the mirror's cluster via `FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS`.
76	
77	Nothing backs this consumer up — no DLQ, no resync sweep: `repo_refs_v1` is lossy
78	(limits-retention) and a dropped event leaves the mirror stale until the
79	primary's **next push**, which heals it fully — every sync replicates full
80	ref state (the v1 staleness RPO, PLAN rev 11). The operator escape hatch for
81	a stuck-empty mirror is hand-publishing one sync job.
82	
83	### Multi-region routing
84	
85	When `FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS` is set, fanout dials one extra NATS connection
86	per entry and routes mirror-job publishes by `Placement.ClusterID`. Fanout
87	does not create or reconcile any stream — `mirror_git_v1` is owned
88	declaratively by the nack jetstream-controller (fleet `apps/nats-streams`);
89	fanout only publishes. An unmapped cluster_id, or a target stream not present
90	yet, surfaces as a publish error → consumer Naks → JetStream redelivers,
91	giving the operator a chance to fix the map or the target cluster without
92	losing the message.
93	
94	`/readyz` gates on the **local** NATS connection and the upstream pull
95	subscription only. Remote-region connections deliberately don't fail
96	readiness: a dead EU NATS already surfaces as publish errors → consumer
97	Nak → JetStream redelivery (no loss inside the webhook stream's MaxAge),
98	and gating on it would stall every region's mirroring for one region's
99	problem — including crashlooping fanout at boot if a remote was down
100	during a pod restart (remotes now dial with `RetryOnFailedConnect`).
101	Remote connectedness is exported as the `fanout.nats.region_connected`
102	gauge (1/0 per `cluster_id`); alert on `== 0`.
103	
104	Example staging-us-west-2 overlay snippet:
105	
106	```yaml
107	- name: FANOUT_LOCAL_CLUSTER_ID
108	  value: royalcanin
109	- name: FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS
110	  value: eukanuba=tls://nats.eks-staging-eu-west-1.partial.to:4222
111	```
112	
113	Stream replicas, sizing, and retention are no longer fanout's concern — they
114	live on the per-cluster `Stream` CRs managed by the nack controller (fleet
115	`apps/nats-streams`). Fanout reads no `ENTIRE_NATS_*` stream-config env.
116	
117	## Ack semantics
118	
119	- **Ack** on successful dispatch, and on benign no-ops (the native-mirror
120	  consumer tags these on its completed metric: `tlog_ref`, `not_home`,
121	  `no_native_mirrors`, `repo_not_found`).
122	- **Term** on bad envelope (cannot unmarshal `ForwardedWebhook` /
123	  `RefEvent`) or dispatcher input error (bad JSON, invalid `full_name`).
124	- **Nak** (with a flat 30s delay, `consumerFailureDelay`) on any other
125	  dispatch error — `MaxDeliver` 8 (~3.5m in-stream), then on the final
126	  delivery the webhook is captured to the DLQ and Term'd. The
127	  native-mirror consumer has no DLQ: an
128	  exhausted ref event is simply dropped and healed by the next push.
129	
130	## Why the two-stage split
131	
132	See `docs/multi-region/multi-region-fanout-design.md` and
133	`docs/multi-region/multi-region-fanout-impl-plan.md`.
134

With the native-mirror consumer enabled, every overlay must carry the full remote map — an empty map silently publishes cross-cluster jobs to local NATS, where no worker consumes their subject. |

¹ Required only when the webhook consumer is enabled.
² Required when `FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS` is set, or when the native-mirror
consumer is enabled.

`FANOUT_DURABLE` must be distinct per region (e.g. `fanout-us-east-2`,
`fanout-eu-central-1`). JetStream durables are stream-scoped; sharing one
across regions on the same upstream stream collapses the consumers. The
native-mirror consumer's durable is fixed (`native-mirror-fanout`) instead:
its stream is per-cluster local, so no two clusters can collide.

## Native-mirror trigger (COR-1021)

Each cluster's entiredb publishes one `repo_refs_v1` event per committed ref
change on any repo it hosts. The native-mirror consumer:

1. skips `refs/tlog/*` churn (the branch event already triggers the sync);
2. resolves the event's repo id through the cached
   `Core.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID`;
3. **drops the event unless this cluster is the repo group's git-data home**
   — loop prevention: a worker push into a native-mirror placement echoes on
   THAT cluster's stream, and without the home check a sync would trigger
   another sync;
4. publishes one `sync_repo` job (`SourceKindEntireDB`, `Source.URL` = the
   home cluster's internal by-ID git URL) per serving native mirror, routed
   to the mirror's cluster via `FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS`.

Nothing backs this consumer up — no DLQ, no resync sweep: `repo_refs_v1` is lossy
(limits-retention) and a dropped event leaves the mirror stale until the
primary's **next push**, which heals it fully — every sync replicates full
ref state (the v1 staleness RPO, PLAN rev 11). The operator escape hatch for
a stuck-empty mirror is hand-publishing one sync job.

### Multi-region routing

When `FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS` is set, fanout dials one extra NATS connection
per entry and routes mirror-job publishes by `Placement.ClusterID`. Fanout
does not create or reconcile any stream — `mirror_git_v1` is owned
declaratively by the nack jetstream-controller (fleet `apps/nats-streams`);
fanout only publishes. An unmapped cluster_id, or a target stream not present
yet, surfaces as a publish error → consumer Naks → JetStream redelivers,
giving the operator a chance to fix the map or the target cluster without
losing the message.

`/readyz` gates on the **local** NATS connection and the upstream pull
subscription only. Remote-region connections deliberately don't fail
readiness: a dead EU NATS already surfaces as publish errors → consumer
Nak → JetStream redelivery (no loss inside the webhook stream's MaxAge),
and gating on it would stall every region's mirroring for one region's
problem — including crashlooping fanout at boot if a remote was down
during a pod restart (remotes now dial with `RetryOnFailedConnect`).
Remote connectedness is exported as the `fanout.nats.region_connected`
gauge (1/0 per `cluster_id`); alert on `== 0`.

Example staging-us-west-2 overlay snippet:

```yaml
- name: FANOUT_LOCAL_CLUSTER_ID
  value: royalcanin
- name: FANOUT_NATS_REGIONS
  value: eukanuba=tls://nats.eks-staging-eu-west-1.partial.to:4222
```

Stream replicas, sizing, and retention are no longer fanout's concern — they
live on the per-cluster `Stream` CRs managed by the nack controller (fleet
`apps/nats-streams`). Fanout reads no `ENTIRE_NATS_*` stream-config env.

## Ack semantics

- **Ack** on successful dispatch, and on benign no-ops (the native-mirror
  consumer tags these on its completed metric: `tlog_ref`, `not_home`,
  `no_native_mirrors`, `repo_not_found`).
- **Term** on bad envelope (cannot unmarshal `ForwardedWebhook` /
  `RefEvent`) or dispatcher input error (bad JSON, invalid `full_name`).
- **Nak** (with a flat 30s delay, `consumerFailureDelay`) on any other
  dispatch error — `MaxDeliver` 8 (~3.5m in-stream), then on the final
  delivery the webhook is captured to the DLQ and Term'd. The
  native-mirror consumer has no DLQ: an
  exhausted ref event is simply dropped and healed by the next push.

## Why the two-stage split

See `docs/multi-region/multi-region-fanout-design.md` and
`docs/multi-region/multi-region-fanout-impl-plan.md`.

89	// refEventDecoder turns a raw repo_refs_v1 delivery into the engine envelope.
90	// A decode failure → Term (bad envelope). Event carries the ref op so the
91	// completed metric's event attribute stays low-cardinality: the KNOWN wire
92	// vocabulary (create/update/delete/force_update/symref_update) passes
93	// through, anything else is clamped to "other" — Unmarshal tolerates
94	// newer-producer payloads by design, so the wire value is unbounded even
95	// though the payload is valid. DeliveryID is the producer's
96	// content+timestamp identity, which doubles as the engine's route-memo key.
97	type refEventDecoder struct{}
98	
99	// eventOther stands in for a ref op outside the known vocabulary on the
100	// metric attribute, so a future producer op can't create unbounded metric
101	// cardinality. Spans/logs still carry the real op via the resolver.
102	const eventOther = "other"
103	
104	var knownRefOps = map[string]bool{
105		refevents.RefOpCreate:       true,
106		refevents.RefOpUpdate:       true,
107		refevents.RefOpDelete:       true,
108		refevents.RefOpForceUpdate:  true,
109		refevents.RefOpSymrefUpdate: true,
110	}

112	func (refEventDecoder) Decode(data []byte) (fanoutengine.Envelope, error) {
113		ev, err := refevents.Unmarshal(data)
114		if err != nil {
115			return fanoutengine.Envelope{}, err
116		}
117		event := ev.RefOp
118		if !knownRefOps[event] {
119			event = eventOther
120		}

122			Event:      event,
123			DeliveryID: ev.DeliveryID(),
124			ObservedAt: ev.Timestamp,
125			Body:       data,
126		}, nil

135		)

163	// For a native-mirror group every ref op fans out — hash transitions move

171	func (d *nativeMirrorSyncResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context, _ string, _ string, _ time.Time, body []byte) ([]fanoutengine.Route, string, error) {
172		ev, err := refevents.Unmarshal(body)
173		if err != nil {
174			// Unreachable in practice — Decode already validated this payload —
175			// kept as an input error so a future decoder/resolver drift Terms
176			// instead of redelivering a poison payload forever.
177			return nil, "", fanoutengine.Input("invalid ref event: %v", err)
178		}
179		if ev.RepoID == "" {
180			// Unmarshal tolerates absent fields by design (independent producer
181			// deploys), but an event with no repo id can never resolve — an
182			// input error (Term), not a Nak, or the poison payload would ride
183			// all MaxDeliver redeliveries for nothing.
184			return nil, "", fanoutengine.Input("ref event has no repo_id")
185		}
186	
187		if strings.HasPrefix(ev.RefName, "refs/tlog/") {
188			return nil, ackReasonTlogRef, nil
189		}
190	
191		// Stamp the parent span with the source coordinates so dropped or failed
192		// deliveries are still findable by repo id. entire.ref_event.op is
193		// re-stamped with the WIRE value: the decoder's envelope clamps unknown
194		// ops to "other" for metric cardinality, but the span can carry the
195		// real one.
196		span := trace.SpanFromContext(ctx)
197		span.SetAttributes(
198			attribute.String("entire.source_kind", "entiredb"),
199			attribute.String("entire.repo_id", ev.RepoID),
200			attribute.String("entire.ref_name", ev.RefName),
201			attribute.String("entire.ref_event.op", ev.RefOp),
202		)
203	
204		res, err := d.routes.NativeMirrorRoutes(ctx, ev.RepoID)
205		if err != nil {
206			if errors.Is(err, mirrorjobs.ErrNativeRepoNotFound) {
207				// Repo deleted between event publish and consume: benign skip.
208				span.AddEvent("native_mirror.repo_not_found")
209				slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Ref event for unknown repo; skipping",
210					slog.String("repo_id", ev.RepoID), slog.String("ref_name", ev.RefName))
211				return nil, ackReasonRepoNotFound, nil
212			}
213			slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Native mirror route resolution failed",
214				slog.String("repo_id", ev.RepoID), slog.Any("error", err))
215			return nil, "", err
216		}
217	
218		if res.HomeClusterID != d.localClusterID {
219			// Mirror-side echo of a worker push (or an event for a repo homed
220			// elsewhere): only the home cluster fans out.
221			span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("entire.native_mirror.home_cluster_id", res.HomeClusterID))
222			return nil, ackReasonNotHome, nil
223		}
224	
225		if len(res.NamespaceRoutes) > 0 && !strings.HasPrefix(ev.RefName, namespaceRefPrefix) {
226			return nil, ackReasonNamespaceOutOfScope, nil
227		}
228	
229		routes := slices.Concat(res.Routes, res.NamespaceRoutes)
230		if len(routes) == 0 {
231			return nil, ackReasonNoMirrors, nil
232		}
233	
234		out := make([]fanoutengine.Route, 0, len(routes))
235		for _, route := range routes {
236			out = append(out, gitSyncRoute{route: route})
237		}
238		return out, "", nil
239	}

2	// repo_refs_v1 wire contract (entiredb refevents/refevents.go — the source
3	// of truth, which owns the stream, the producer sinks, and the full RefEvent
4	// format). This copy exists so mirror-pipeline can decode ref events without
5	// taking a Go-module dependency on the entiredb tree, the same trade the
6	// repository-local repolookup proto copy makes. Keep the stream/subject names
7	// and the JSON field names byte-for-byte identical with entiredb's copy — they
8	// are the on-the-wire contract and any drift silently breaks the consumer.
9	//
10	// The stream is per-cluster and LOCAL: every entiredb cluster publishes its
11	// own repo_refs_v1 onto its own NATS island, one event per committed ref
12	// change on any repo hosted there. Producers guarantee at-least-once
13	// delivery of committed changes (transactional outbox), but the stream is
14	// limits-retention and its history is bounded — a consumer that needs
15	// correctness beyond the retention window must get it elsewhere (for native
16	// mirroring: every sync replicates full ref state, so the next push heals a
17	// lost event).
18	package refevents
19	
20	import (
21		"bytes"
22		"encoding/json"
23		"errors"
24		"fmt"
25		"time"
26	)
27	
28	// NATS stream / subject identity, as declared by entiredb (the stream owner).
29	// Events are published on NATSSubjectPrefix + <repo ULID>.
30	const (
31		NATSSubjectPrefix = "repo_refs_v1."
32		NATSStreamName    = "repo_refs_v1"
33	)
34	
35	// refEventVersion is the supported wire envelope version.
36	const refEventVersion = 1
37	
38	// Wire values for RefEvent.RefOp.
39	const (
40		RefOpCreate      = "create"
41		RefOpUpdate      = "update"
42		RefOpDelete      = "delete"
43		RefOpForceUpdate = "force_update"
44		// RefOpSymrefUpdate is a symbolic ref retargeting (today only HEAD, moved
45		// on a default-branch change). It carries no object motion: the targets
46		// stay empty and the transition is OldSymrefTarget → NewSymrefTarget.
47		RefOpSymrefUpdate = "symref_update"
48	)
49	
50	// RefEvent is the JSON wire format for ref-change notifications on
51	// repo_refs_v1. Only the fields this repo's consumers read are declared;
52	// unknown fields are tolerated by Unmarshal (producers deploy independently).
53	type RefEvent struct {
54		Version       int       `json:"version"`
55		RepoID        string    `json:"repo_id"`
56		RefName       string    `json:"ref_name"`
57		RefOp         string    `json:"ref_op"`
58		OldTarget     string    `json:"old_target"`
59		NewTarget     string    `json:"new_target"`
60		HashAlgorithm string    `json:"hash_algorithm"`
61		Timestamp     time.Time `json:"timestamp"`
62		// OldSymrefTarget/NewSymrefTarget carry a symbolic ref's retargeting for
63		// RefOpSymrefUpdate events (full ref names, e.g. "refs/heads/main" →
64		// "refs/heads/studio"). Empty on every hash-transition op.
65		OldSymrefTarget string `json:"old_symref_target,omitempty"`
66		NewSymrefTarget string `json:"new_symref_target,omitempty"`
67	}
68	
69	// Unmarshal decodes a JSON ref event from its NATS payload.
70	//
71	// Unknown fields are tolerated deliberately: producers (entiredb nodes) and
72	// this consumer deploy independently, so payloads from a publisher one
73	// version ahead of or behind the decoder are normal, not malformed. The
74	// version field is the gate for genuinely breaking envelope changes.
75	func Unmarshal(data []byte) (RefEvent, error) {
76		var ev RefEvent
77		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
78		if err := dec.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
79			return RefEvent{}, fmt.Errorf("decode ref event: %w", err)
80		}
81		if dec.More() {
82			return RefEvent{}, errors.New("trailing data after ref event")
83		}
84		if ev.Version != refEventVersion {
85			return RefEvent{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported ref event version: %d", ev.Version)
86		}
87		return ev, nil
88	}
89	
90	// DeliveryID identifies one emitted event: the ref-transition content scoped
91	// by the emit timestamp — the same identity the producer uses as its outbox
92	// Nats-Msg-Id, so a JetStream redelivery of one emit carries the same value
93	// while a later re-push of the same transition gets a fresh one. Consumers
94	// use it as their per-delivery dedup/memo key.
95	func (ev RefEvent) DeliveryID() string {
96		old, next := ev.OldTarget, ev.NewTarget
97		if ev.RefOp == RefOpSymrefUpdate {
98			// A symref move carries no hashes; its transition is the ref-name
99			// pair. Ref names cannot contain ':', so the format stays unambiguous.
100			old, next = ev.OldSymrefTarget, ev.NewSymrefTarget
101		}
102		return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s:%s:%s:%d", ev.RepoID, ev.RefName, old, next, ev.Timestamp.UnixNano())
103	}

1	package main
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"net/http"
8		"net/url"
9		"time"
10	
11		"entire.io/entire/git-sync"
12		"go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/net/http/otelhttp"
13		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute"
14		otelcodes "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
15		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
16	
17		"github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/pkg/gitjobs"
18	)
19	
20	// maxSyncAttempts bounds in-process retries for transient git-fetch failures.
21	// Production measurement over 14 days of @entire.sync.attempts on mirror.sync
22	// spans showed attempt 1 = 147,132 syncs, attempt 2 = 3,573 (2.4% of attempt 1
23	// continued), attempt 3 = 862 (24% of attempt 2 continued) — under the old
24	// 3-attempt budget, that attempt-3 tail left ~1.2 terminal 404s/day. The two
25	// continuation rates differ by an order of magnitude, so the decay beyond
26	// attempt 3 isn't known and a precise residual-failure estimate at 8 attempts
27	// isn't supported by this data; widening the budget is expected to clear
28	// materially more of the attempt-3 tail without a confident number attached.
29	const maxSyncAttempts = 8
30	
31	// syncRetryDelay paces in-process retries. The shortest observed gap between
32	// a 404 and a successful sibling sync of the same repo was ~3s, so a 2s
33	// delay sits just under that boundary — long enough for GitHub's git edge
34	// to settle after a mint, short enough to stay responsive. Kept fixed (no
35	// exponential backoff): the continuation rates behind maxSyncAttempts were
36	// measured at this exact spacing, so changing it would invalidate that data.
37	const syncRetryDelay = 2 * time.Second
38	
39	// unmirroredRefPrefix marks branches that live only in Entire and are never
40	// mirrored to/from GitHub. Excluding it from the sync scope also excludes it
41	// from prune, so a GitHub→Entire sync can't delete an unmirrored branch that
42	// (by definition) has no counterpart on the source. This is the inbound half
43	// of the contract; the outbound half (skipping push-through) lives in
44	// entiredb's server/githttp. entiredb pins the same literal as
45	// mirror.UnmirroredRefPrefix — kept in lockstep here because the two live in
46	// separate Go modules. See entiredb docs/adrs/20260702-unmirrored-branches.md.
47	const unmirroredRefPrefix = "refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/"
48	
49	// namespaceRefPrefix is the Entire-owned ref namespace (COR-1563). entiredb's
50	// writer scope refuses a push to it that does not declare the namespace sync
51	// kind, so a GitHub-kind sync — AllRefs + prune — must exclude it, or it plans
52	// a delete of every namespace ref the target holds and fails on every
53	// redelivery. entiredb pins the same literal as forge.NativeRefPrefix; kept in
54	// lockstep here because the two live in separate Go modules.
55	const namespaceRefPrefix = "refs/heads/entire/native/"
56	
57	// reservedAncestorRefs are the bare directory-anchor refs entiredb blocks from
58	// creation so the namespace beneath each stays usable: a leaf ref squatting an
59	// anchor would directory/file-conflict with every ref under it. entiredb
60	// rejects a push to any of them, so the worker must skip them on inbound sync
61	// or a source repo that happens to carry one would fail the whole mirror.
62	// These are exact-match (ExcludeRefs), NOT prefixes, so a normal ref like
63	// refs/heads/entire/a or refs/meta/entire/main still passes this filter.
64	//
65	// The refs/heads/* pair protects the unmirrored-branches feature (entiredb
66	// docs/adrs/20260702-unmirrored-branches.md); the refs/meta pair are base
67	// anchors entiredb reserves for EVERY caller — a workload carve-out matches by
68	// prefix + "/" and so never reaches the bare anchor. Keep in lockstep with the
69	// reservedExact set in entiredb's refpolicy/refpolicy.go.
70	var reservedAncestorRefs = []string{
71		"refs/heads/entire",
72		"refs/heads/entire/unmirrored",
73		"refs/meta",
74		"refs/meta/entire",
75	}
76	
77	// excludeRefPrefixes are the source ref namespaces the worker never mirrors
78	// (and, being unmirrored, never prunes) on a GITHUB sync. Shared between the
79	// sync scope and the default-branch reconcile guard: a source HEAD under one
80	// of these prefixes can never land on the target, so the reconcile treats it
81	// as non-convergent rather than looping forever (see isNonMirrorableBranch —
82	// which deliberately keeps checking THIS list for both kinds, because
83	// entiredb's SetDefaultBranch rejects an unmirrored-namespace default
84	// unconditionally). The refs/heads/ entries here are the only ones a HEAD
85	// could point at; the rest are kept for a single source of truth with the
86	// sync scope. entiredb-kind syncs use excludeRefPrefixesFor, which drops
87	// exactly one entry.
88	var excludeRefPrefixes = []string{
89		"refs/pull/",
90		"refs/heads/trunk-merge/",
91		"refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/",
92		"refs/tlog/",

158	// excludeRefPrefixesFor returns the sync-scope exclusions for a source kind.
159	// A GitHub-kind sync additionally excludes the Entire-owned namespace (see
160	// githubExcludeRefPrefixes). An entiredb-kind sync (native mirroring) drops
161	// exactly the unmirrored-namespace exclusion and nothing else (plan decision
162	// 3, ADR 20260720-native-mirroring): that exclusion exists to keep Entire-only
163	// branches out of a GitHub round-trip, and when the source IS entiredb the
164	// namespace replicates like any branch — a native mirror is a full read-only
165	// copy. Everything else stays excluded for the same reasons as GitHub:
166	// refs/tlog/* is per-placement entiredb-owned state receive-pack rejects,
167	// and the reserved namespaces would 403 the push.
168	func excludeRefPrefixesFor(kind gitjobs.SourceKind) []string {
169		if kind == gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDBNamespace {
170			// Scoped by inclusion, not exclusion: every ref outside the namespace is
171			// already out of scope, including git-sync's own bootstrap markers,
172			// which take their scope from the branch they checkpoint.
173			return nil
174		}
175		if kind != gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB {
176			return githubExcludeRefPrefixes
177		}
178		out := make([]string, 0, len(excludeRefPrefixes)-1)
179		for _, p := range excludeRefPrefixes {
180			if p != unmirroredRefPrefix {
181				out = append(out, p)
182			}
183		}
184		return out
185	}

228		// SourceKind selects the source leg: github (owner/repo against
229		// sourceBaseURL, App-token auth) or entiredb (SourceURL, cert-only).
230		// The zero value means github so existing callers/tests read unchanged.
231		SourceKind     gitjobs.SourceKind
232		SourceOwner    string
233		SourceRepo     string

236		// cluster. SourceClusterParent is the consume-time admitted transport
237		// boundary; the syncer must not derive certificate routing from SourceURL.
238		// Both are entiredb-kind only.

483		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Starting git-sync",
484			slog.String("source_kind", string(req.kind())),
485			slog.String("source", sourceURL),
486			slog.String("target", targetURL),
487			slog.Int64("installation_id", req.InstallationID),
488		)
489	
490		auth, err := s.sourceAuth(ctx, req)
491		if err != nil {
492			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Int("entire.sync.attempts", 1))
493			classified := classifySyncError(fmt.Errorf("resolving source auth: %w", err))
494			span.RecordError(classified)
495			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "source auth")
496			return classified
497		}

499		// The token is minted once and reused across retries: the working theory
500		// for the transient 404 is GitHub's eventual consistency between
501		// api.github.com (where the token is minted) and github.com (where the
502		// git fetch uses it). Waiting lets that token propagate. Re-minting
503		// would reset the propagation clock with a fresh token, defeating the
504		// purpose of the backoff.
505		client := gitsync.New(gitsync.Options{
506			HTTPClient:                    s.httpClientFor(req),
507			BootstrapFallbackMaxPackBytes: s.bootstrapFallbackMaxPackBytes,
508			Auth:                          auth,
509			BootstrapLogger: slog.Default().With(
510				slog.String("target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
511				slog.String("source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
512				slog.String("source_repo", req.SourceRepo)),
513		})

515		replicateReq := gitsync.SyncRequest{
516			// An entiredb source cluster 307s /info/refs off a non-hosting
517			// node exactly like the target does, so carry the redirect into
518			// the endpoint for entiredb-kind fetches; GitHub never emits it
519			// and keeps the plain endpoint.
520			Source: gitsync.Endpoint{
521				URL:                    sourceURL,
522				FollowInfoRefsRedirect: req.entiredbSourced(),
523			},
524			// FollowInfoRefsRedirect carries the 307 from a non-hosting
525			// entiredb node into the endpoint, so the subsequent
526			// receive-pack POST lands on the hosting replica instead of
527			// the originally-configured host. No-op for the current
528			// node-specific ENTIRE_TARGET_URL (node1 either hosts or
529			// serves via DISS), but lets us flip fleet to the cluster
530			// entry domain without a code change.
531			Target: gitsync.Endpoint{URL: targetURL, FollowInfoRefsRedirect: true},
532			Scope:  refScopeFor(req),
533			Policy: syncPolicyFor(req),
534		}

536		var (
537			result  gitsync.SyncResult
538			lastErr error
539			attempt int
540		)
541		for attempt = 1; attempt <= maxSyncAttempts; attempt++ {
542			if attempt > 1 {
543				select {
544				case <-ctx.Done():
545					span.SetAttributes(attribute.Int("entire.sync.attempts", attempt-1))
546					classified := transientErr(ctx.Err())
547					reportSyncFailure(ctx, span, result, classified, ctx.Err(), req)
548					span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "context canceled during retry backoff")
549					return classified
550				case <-time.After(syncRetryDelay):
551				}
552			}
553	
554			result, err = client.Replicate(ctx, replicateReq)
555			if err == nil {
556				lastErr = nil
557				break
558			}
559			lastErr = err
560			if !isTransientGitFetchError(err) {
561				break
562			}
563			if attempt >= maxSyncAttempts {
564				break
565			}
566			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "Transient git-fetch failure; will retry",
567				slog.Int("attempt", attempt),
568				slog.Int("max_attempts", maxSyncAttempts),
569				slog.Any("error", redactAuth(err)),
570			)
571		}

573		span.SetAttributes(attribute.Int("entire.sync.attempts", attempt))

575		// A prune delete rejected with entiredb's deny-current-branch reason
576		// means the source renamed its default branch and the mirror's HEAD
577		// hasn't followed: move HEAD via RepoAdmin.SetDefaultBranch, then
578		// re-run the identical replicate in the same job so the stale branch
579		// prunes immediately. This branch is terminal — recovery classifies its
580		// own failures (a transient GitHub 404 during the probe/re-replicate is
581		// retried in-process and stays transient; a non-convergent case such as
582		// an excluded source HEAD or an RPC PermissionDenied is marked permanent
583		// so it stops churning instead of redelivering forever) and returns them
584		// directly, bypassing the generic classifier below. followed tracks that
585		// HEAD was just ensured so the steady-state follow further down skips its
586		// redundant RPC. Already-wedged mirrors heal on their next sync.
587		followed := false
588		if lastErr != nil && s.repoAdmin != nil && !req.namespaceScoped() {
589			if rejectedRef, ok := isDenyCurrentBranchDeletion(lastErr); ok {
590				span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.default_branch_recovery", true))
591				recResult, ensuredHEAD, recErr := s.recoverDefaultBranchRename(ctx, req.TargetULID, rejectedRef,
592					func(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
593						probe, perr := retryTransientFetch(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (gitsync.ProbeResult, error) {
594							return client.Probe(ctx, gitsync.ProbeRequest{Source: gitsync.Endpoint{URL: sourceURL}})
595						})
596						if perr != nil {
597							return "", perr
598						}
599						return probe.SourceHEAD, nil
600					},
601					func(ctx context.Context) (gitsync.SyncResult, error) {
602						return retryTransientFetch(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (gitsync.SyncResult, error) {
603							return client.Replicate(ctx, replicateReq)
604						})
605					},
606				)
607				if recErr != nil {
608					classified := classifyRecoveryError(recErr)
609					span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("entire.sync.default_branch_recovery_error", recoveryErrorCode(recErr)))
610					reportSyncFailure(ctx, span, recoveryReportResult(recResult, result), classified, recErr, req)
611					return classified
612				}
613				result = recResult
614				lastErr = nil
615				// Skip the steady-state follow only when the re-run confirmed the
616				// source HEAD we just ensured. A source that switched its default
617				// AGAIN mid-recovery shows a fresher SourceHEAD on the re-run's
618				// result — fall through to the follow so it is applied now rather
619				// than waiting for the next sync.
620				followed = result.Execution.SourceHEAD == "" || result.Execution.SourceHEAD == ensuredHEAD
621			}
622		}
623	
624		if lastErr != nil {
625			// No refs to apply is a clean no-op, not a failure: don't record it as
626			// a span error and signal the noop disposition so disposeResult acks
627			// rather than redelivering a job that can only repeat the same outcome
628			// against an unchanged source. The reason is recorded but does NOT
629			// change the disposition — every case here acks with no watermark. Only
630			// the diverged case is a standing problem, and it is deliberately
631			// surfaced through the counter and the span rather than through a
632			// failed sync: redelivering it would repeat a refusal that no retry can
633			// resolve, and terminating it would publish 'failed' for a mirror that
634			// is perfectly clonable.
635			if reason, ok := classifyEmptySource(lastErr, req.SourceRefsClaim, req.TargetRefsClaim); ok {
636				// The reason alone is not enough to act on for the uncorroborated
637				// family — one sentinel covers sub-cases with opposite remedies,
638				// separated only by the wrapped message — so the error text rides
639				// on the span and the log, redacted like every other surfaced
640				// sync error.
641				span.SetAttributes(
642					attribute.Bool("entire.sync.noop", true),
643					attribute.String("entire.sync.empty_source_reason", string(reason)),
644					attribute.String("entire.sync.empty_source_error", redactAuth(lastErr).Error()),
645				)
646				span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Ok, "no source refs to apply")
647				logEmptySource(ctx, reason, req, lastErr)
648				s.metrics.recordEmptySource(ctx, reason, req.SourceClusterParent)
649				return errSourceNoRefs
650			}
651			classified := classifySyncError(redactAuth(lastErr))
652			reportSyncFailure(ctx, span, result, classified, lastErr, req)
653			return classified
654		}
655	
656		span.SetAttributes(
657			attribute.Int("entire.refs.applied", result.Counts.Applied),
658			attribute.Int("entire.refs.skipped", result.Counts.Skipped),
659			attribute.Int("entire.refs.blocked", result.Counts.Blocked),
660			attribute.Int("entire.refs.deleted", result.Counts.Deleted),
661		)
662	
663		s.reportSyncSuccess(ctx, result, req)
664	
665		// Steady-state follow: a default-branch change to an already-existing
666		// branch produces no data-plane push, so it only ever surfaces here —
667		// as the source HEAD git-sync parsed during the sync. Idempotent
668		// server-side and best-effort (a failure defers to the next sync);
669		// skipped when the recovery path above already ensured HEAD.
670		if !followed && !req.namespaceScoped() {
671			s.followSourceHEAD(ctx, req.TargetULID, result.Execution.SourceHEAD)
672		}
673	
674		return nil
675	}

677	// markSyncSpanResult records a failed sync on the mirror.sync span — except for
678	// a benign concurrent-ref race, which lost a compare-and-swap to a competing
679	// sync of the same repo and self-heals on the next delivery. A race is tagged
680	// entire.sync.raced (queryable, mirroring the mirror.consume carve-out) but left
681	// un-errored, so it never shows as a failed mirror.sync span or counts toward an
682	// error-rate query on this span — matching the outcome metric's nak+term
683	// numerator, which also excludes raced. Exhaustion is a delivery-count concept
684	// the syncer can't see; the consumer still escalates a race that burns through
685	// redelivery to an error on the parent mirror.consume span (see
686	// shouldMarkSpanError). The race check uses the raw error, not the
687	// redacted/classified one, so redactAuth flattening the chain can't defeat it.
688	func markSyncSpanResult(span trace.Span, classified, raw error) {
689		if isConcurrentRefError(raw) {
690			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.raced", true))
691			return
692		}
693		span.RecordError(classified)
694		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "sync from github")
695	}

697	// recoveryReportResult picks which result is worth reporting when the
698	// default-branch reconcile fails.
699	//
700	// Every guard in recoverDefaultBranchRename that bails before re-running
701	// replicate returns a zero SyncResult, so reporting it would log empty
702	// execution attributes and erase the route of the sync that triggered the
703	// reconcile — the one fact reportSyncFailure exists to preserve. The re-run's
704	// result is preferred when it actually ran; otherwise the original failure's
705	// route stands, which is the sync an operator is trying to understand anyway.
706	func recoveryReportResult(recResult, original gitsync.SyncResult) gitsync.SyncResult {
707		if recResult.Execution.OperationMode != "" {
708			return recResult
709		}
710		return original
711	}

715	// route that selected bootstrap and the reason relay was unavailable; dropping
716	// the result here made those failures indistinguishable from an ordinary relay
717	// failure in both logs and traces.
718	func reportSyncFailure(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, result gitsync.SyncResult, classified, raw error, req syncRequest) {
719		span.SetAttributes(
720			attribute.String("entire.sync.operation_mode", result.Execution.OperationMode),
721			attribute.String("entire.sync.transfer_mode", result.Execution.TransferMode),
722			attribute.String("entire.sync.relay_reason", result.Execution.Reason),
723			attribute.Bool("entire.sync.batch.enabled", result.Execution.Batch.Enabled),
724			attribute.Int("entire.sync.batch.planned", result.Execution.Batch.Planned),
725			attribute.Int("entire.sync.batch.done", result.Execution.Batch.Done),
726		)
727		markSyncSpanResult(span, classified, raw)
728	
729		args := []any{
730			slog.String("source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
731			slog.String("source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
732			slog.String("target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
733			slog.String("operation_mode", result.Execution.OperationMode),
734			slog.String("transfer_mode", result.Execution.TransferMode),
735			slog.String("relay_reason", result.Execution.Reason),
736			slog.Bool("batch_enabled", result.Execution.Batch.Enabled),
737			slog.Int("batch_planned", result.Execution.Batch.Planned),
738			slog.Int("batch_done", result.Execution.Batch.Done),
739			slog.Any("error", classified),
740		}

745		slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "Git sync execution failed", args...)

778	// reportSyncSuccess records a completed sync's outcome: the log line, and for a
779	// converged empty pair the counter reason that says the placement healed.
780	//
781	// Extracted from sync() for one reason — nothing could test it there. The
782	// converged branch is the only reason this change exists, and it is invisible
783	// to the compiler and to every existing test: deleting it left the whole suite
784	// green, because the position still gets stamped by the ordinary success path
785	// (err == nil), so the only casualties were the counter and the log. Those are
786	// exactly the signal COR-1300 was filed to produce, and they would have gone
787	// quiet with nothing failing.
788	//
789	// Takes the span from ctx rather than as a parameter so a test can call it with
790	// a plain context and get a no-op span, matching the replicate-thunk seam
791	// recoverDefaultBranchRename already uses for the same reason.
792	func (s *syncer) reportSyncSuccess(ctx context.Context, result gitsync.SyncResult, req syncRequest) {
793		if result.Execution.Converged {
794			// Source asserted empty, target asserted empty, and git-sync
795			// corroborated both in one session: converged with nothing to apply.
796			// Reported as a real success rather than a no-op BECAUSE the coverage
797			// is provable, which is what lets the completion carry a write
798			// position — the thing that clears a resync flag on a repo that was
799			// created and never pushed to.
800			trace.SpanFromContext(ctx).SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.converged", true))
801			s.metrics.recordEmptySource(ctx, emptyReasonConverged, req.SourceClusterParent)
802			slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Sync complete: source and target both empty, nothing to mirror",
803				slog.String("source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
804				slog.String("source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
805				slog.String("target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
806			)
807			return
808		}
809		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "Sync complete",
810			slog.String("source_owner", req.SourceOwner),
811			slog.String("source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
812			slog.String("target_ulid", req.TargetULID),
813			slog.Int("applied", result.Counts.Applied),
814			slog.Int("skipped", result.Counts.Skipped),
815			slog.Int("blocked", result.Counts.Blocked),
816			slog.Int("deleted", result.Counts.Deleted),
817			// The strategy git-sync actually chose. Routing decisions (replicate
818			// vs bootstrap vs bootstrap resume) were previously invisible here,
819			// which is why ENT-2054 took a code read instead of a log query.
820			slog.String("operation_mode", result.Execution.OperationMode),
821			slog.String("transfer_mode", result.Execution.TransferMode),
822			slog.String("relay_reason", result.Execution.Reason),
823		)
824	}

826	// refScopeFor builds the ref scope for one request. Extracted alongside
827	// syncPolicyFor because AllRefs is not merely this worker's preference: it is a
828	// precondition git-sync enforces for the empty-source policy (under a narrower
829	// scope the source listing is itself narrowed, so an empty result says nothing
830	// about the repository), and a scope built inline in the config literal is one
831	// no test can read.
832	func refScopeFor(req syncRequest) gitsync.RefScope {
833		return gitsync.RefScope{
834			AllRefs: true,
835			// refs/pull/* is GitHub's PR ref namespace — skip mirroring it
836			// to avoid surfacing source-side PR state on the mirror.
837			//
838			// refs/heads/trunk-merge/* and refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/*
839			// are ephemeral merge-queue refs (trunk-merge keyed by PR number
840			// + a per-attempt UUID; gh-readonly-queue is GitHub's native
841			// merge-queue namespace, refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/<base>/
842			// pr-<n>-<sha>): created and deleted within minutes, so mirroring
843			// them is pure churn. Because each is brand-new, git-sync plans a
844			// create (target hash zero) that races a concurrent webhook or the
845			// re-kicker and draws entire-server's create-side CAS rejection
846			// ("already exists"). They carry no value on the mirror, so we drop
847			// them at the source rather than push and prune the churn. (The
848			// create-race misclassification itself is now fixed upstream:
849			// git-sync classifies "already exists" as ErrTargetRefMoved — the
850			// create-side analog of "remote ref has changed" — so a create race
851			// that still slips through routes to dispositionRaced like any
852			// concurrent-ref miss rather than a hard sync failure; see
853			// isConcurrentRefError. This exclusion just removes the dominant
854			// source of those redeliveries.)
855			//
856			// The remaining prefixes mirror entiredb's reserved-push denylist
857			// (the reservedPrefixes/reservedExact sets in its refpolicy
858			// package, applied by server/githttp receive-pack):
859			// git-receive-pack returns 403 "push to <ref> is not allowed"
860			// for any of these namespaces. Under AllRefs we faithfully copy
861			// whatever the source advertises, so a stray ref like
862			// refs/remotes/origin/* accidentally pushed up to a source repo
863			// would otherwise fail the entire sync permanently. Excluding
864			// the prefixes here means we neither read them from the source
865			// nor try to push/prune them on the target.
866			//
867			// refs/tlog/* is entiredb-owned (commit-tlog state appended by
868			// entire-server on its receive-pack hook); direct pushes are
869			// rejected with "use sync instead".
870			//
871			// Per-kind: an entiredb source (native mirroring) additionally
872			// syncs the unmirrored namespace — see excludeRefPrefixesFor.
873			ExcludeRefPrefixes: excludeRefPrefixesFor(req.kind()),
874			// Exact-match reservations (not prefixes): skip the bare
875			// directory-anchor refs entiredb blocks, without excluding
876			// their mirrored children (refs/heads/entire/a still syncs).
877			ExcludeRefs: excludeRefsFor(req.kind()),
878			// The namespace kind is scoped by inclusion: every ref outside the
879			// Entire-owned namespace is neither pushed nor pruned, whatever the
880			// payload claims.
881			IncludeRefPrefixes: includeRefPrefixesFor(req.kind()),
882		}
883	}
884	
885	// syncPolicyFor builds the git-sync policy for one request. Extracted from the
886	// config literal so the empty-source wiring is unit-testable: every field here
887	// is a plain bool with a defaulted-off zero value, so dropping any one of them
888	// compiles, passes, and silently turns the policy off — which is exactly how
889	// the first version of this shipped inert (AllowEmptySource set, the two
890	// assertions it requires never supplied).
891	func syncPolicyFor(req syncRequest) gitsync.SyncPolicy {
892		// entiredb-kind only, for both halves of the empty-source policy. The
893		// distinction is only sound where a data plane can answer for the
894		// repository's ref state, and the watermark it feeds exists solely for
895		// native mirrors — a GitHub source gains nothing and would have its
896		// empty-repo syncs reclassified from no-op to ref-applying success,
897		// moving last_success_unix and pruning the failure index on a sync that
898		// applied nothing.
899		// The namespace kind is excluded with GitHub: it takes no position
900		// snapshot, so it can assert nothing about either leg.
901		native := req.kind() == gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB
902		return gitsync.SyncPolicy{
903			IncludeTags: true,
904			Prune:       true,
905			// Ask git-sync to separate "the source has no refs" from "the scope
906			// selected none of them", and to treat a source and target both
907			// VERIFIED empty as the converged state they are rather than an
908			// error. That converged sync stamps a write position, which is what
909			// lets entire-core's resync sweep clear a flag on a repo that was
910			// created and never pushed to (COR-1300); without it the placement is
911			// flagged behind forever, since a no-op completion carries no
912			// watermark and the flag can never be satisfied.
913			AllowEmptySource: native,
914			// An owner that deleted its last namespace branch advertises refs but
915			// none in scope; without this the replicas keep serving a branch the
916			// owner no longer has.
917			AllowEmptyScope: req.namespaceScoped(),
918			// The assertions git-sync requires before it will call anything
919			// converged: it cannot determine emptiness itself on either leg,
920			// because ref hiding is invisible to a client and configured
921			// independently per leg, so an empty advertisement and a repository
922			// full of hidden refs are the same observation. They come from
923			// RepoAdmin.GetWritePosition on each side, read before the fetch (see
924			// syncRequest).
925			//
926			// git-sync treats them as necessary and never sufficient: it still
927			// requires an empty advertisement on each leg, an unborn HEAD on the
928			// source, and no visible in-scope target ref, and each of those checks
929			// can only refuse. So a wrong assertion cannot manufacture a
930			// convergence out of a populated repository — but a MISSING one
931			// (every read failure lands there) does forfeit a real convergence,
932			// which is the direction to fail in.
933			//
934			// Gated on native as well, so a GitHub request carrying stray
935			// assertions cannot half-enable a policy whose other half is off.
936			SourceAssertedEmpty: native && req.sourceAssertedEmpty(),
937			TargetAssertedEmpty: native && req.targetAssertedEmpty(),
938		}
939	}
940	
941	func (s *syncer) targetURL(req syncRequest) string {
942		return fmt.Sprintf("%s/git/repo/%s", s.targetBaseURL, req.TargetULID)
943	}

946	// entiredb sources never mint: the worker's client certificate is the whole
947	// credential (the source cluster's svctok listener grants the workload
948	// cert-only cluster-wide pull), and clusterTransport already routes the
949	// fetch onto the mTLS round-tripper — a nil provider attaches no header.
950	// For GitHub, returns nil when the job has no installation ID or the App
951	// client is not configured — callers fall through to anonymous GitHub
952	// access for public repos.

954		if req.entiredbSourced() {
955			return nil, nil
956		}

959		}

962			trace.WithAttributes(

964				attribute.String("entire.source_repo", req.SourceRepo),
965			),
966		)
967		defer span.End()

969		// Time exactly the mint round-trip. This is the most actionable git-op
970		// breakdown leg (a synchronous entire-core STS call on every authenticated
971		// sync) and the before/after baseline for COR-596 token caching. Tagged
972		// ok|error only — the failure breakdown lives on this span, not the metric.
973		start := time.Now()
974		token, err := s.githubApp.InstallationToken(ctx, req.TargetULID, req.SourceOwner, req.SourceRepo, req.InstallationID)
975		if err != nil {
976			s.metrics.recordSourceAuth(ctx, sourceAuthOutcomeError, time.Since(start))
977			span.RecordError(err)
978			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "installation token")
979			// Returned unwrapped exactly as before: the sole caller (sync) wraps it
980			// with "resolving source auth: %w" and runs it through classifySyncError,
981			// and the token-leak guard (TestSyncDoesNotLeakInstallationToken) depends
982			// on that path — re-wrapping here would change the error text under it for
983			// no benefit.

The two flags are mutually exclusive. Without either, divergent or
non-ancestor refs are reported as blocked and the sync exits non-zero
before any push, so the lease check is a second line of defense against

force flag to opt out of.

(it never sent a zero expected-old), so the closest direct replacement is
`--force-with-lease`. `--force-blind` is new behavior with no pre-0.5
analog.
