1	// Package refpolicy is the single source of truth for how entiredb treats the
2	// reserved and internal Git ref namespaces. It answers three questions that
3	// were previously decided in three places and drifted:
4	//
5	//   - Push: may this caller push this ref, or is the namespace reserved?
6	//     (was server/githttp/receive_pack.go's reservedPush* slices)
7	//   - Fetch: is this ref hidden from advertisement for this caller?
8	//     (uploadpack.hideRefs, previously wired nil everywhere)
9	//   - Recording: should a push to this ref produce a signed RSL entry?
10	//     (was rslstore.ShouldRecord's denylist)
11	//
12	// Recording starts from fetch visibility: a hidden ref is never signed. Two
13	// visible namespaces are carved out as well. Unmirrored branches
14	// (refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/*) stay visible on fetch but are never mirrored
15	// to GitHub, and git-sync's transfer scaffolding (refs/gitsync/**) stays visible
16	// so a bootstrap can resume but exists only on a replication target (see
17	// ShouldRecord). The coverage mode then narrows what remains to branches, tags,
18	// and checkpoints (see CoveredByMode). Deriving visibility and the recording
19	// base from one hidden set keeps a hidden ref from ever being signed.
20	//
21	// The policy is layered as a chain of command (see resolve): a base layer of
22	// fleet-wide invariants, then per-domain deltas (native vs GitHub-mirror repos),
23	// then per-caller carve-outs. Each layer may only ADD restrictions; the only
24	// ways to loosen are an explicit workload carve-out (push) or the trusted-reader
25	// exemption (fetch). Deny-by-default, fail-closed.
26	package refpolicy
27	
28	import (
29		"slices"
30		"strings"
31	
32		"entire.io/core/servicetoken"
33		"entire.io/internal/go-git/plumbing/transport/hiderefs"
34		"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/rsl"
35	)
36	
37	// Canonical ref namespaces. These names previously lived as unexported
38	// constants in receive_pack.go, rslstore/writer.go, and refstore; this package
39	// is now their one home.
40	const (
41		// GittufPrefix is gittuf's reserved namespace (RSL, policy, policy-staging,
42		// attestations). entiredb owns it server-side; direct client pushes to any
43		// refs/gittuf/* are refused.
44		GittufPrefix = "refs/gittuf/"
45		// RSLRef is the gittuf Reference State Log, written server-side by rslstore.
46		// Bound to gittuf's own constant so the recording carve-out (ShouldRecord)
47		// cannot drift from the ref gittuf actually writes and start signing the RSL
48		// into itself.
49		RSLRef = rsl.Ref
50		// PolicyStagingRef is gittuf's staging policy ref. gittuf keeps its own copy
51		// unexported (unlike rsl.Ref), so this literal must be kept equal to it by
52		// hand.
53		PolicyStagingRef = "refs/gittuf/policy-staging"
54		// PolicyRef is the repo's root of trust. It is client-visible so clients can
55		// verify against it, so it is neither hidden nor exempt from recording.
56		PolicyRef = "refs/gittuf/policy"
57	
58		// ManagedMetaPrefix is the git-meta service's shared metadata namespace,
59		// reserved for direct client pushes but writable by the entire-api workload.
60		// It is client-visible and recorded.
61		ManagedMetaPrefix = "refs/meta/entire/"
62	
63		// InternalPrefix, LocalPrefix, and EntirePrefix are entiredb-internal
64		// namespaces: reserved from direct client push, hidden from external fetch,
65		// and not recorded. Two sub-namespaces below are exceptions on all three
66		// counts, because a client owns each: EntireCheckpointsPrefix and
67		// EntirePoliciesPrefix. refs/local/* holds node-local refs that never leave
68		// the server, so they are never advertised and users cannot push them.
69		InternalPrefix = "refs/internal"
70		LocalPrefix    = "refs/local"
71		EntirePrefix   = "refs/entire"
72	
73		// HeadsPrefix and TagsPrefix are the two ordinary user-facing namespaces.
74		// They carry no policy of their own here. They exist so the coverage modes
75		// in coverage.go name them from the same place as every other namespace
76		// literal rather than re-spelling them.
77		HeadsPrefix = "refs/heads/"
78		TagsPrefix  = "refs/tags/"
79	
80		// GitSyncScaffoldPrefix is git-sync's own temp-ref namespace on a
81		// replication TARGET: a batched bootstrap parks each branch at
82		// refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch> and removes it when the branch
83		// lands. It is transfer scaffolding the sync writes and deletes itself, not
84		// repository content, and it exists ONLY on the target — the primary never
85		// holds one, so the primary's RSL never attests one.
86		//
87		// It is carved out of recording for that reason, and deliberately NOT hidden:
88		// git-sync reads its own scaffolding back from the target's advertisement to
89		// resume an interrupted bootstrap, so hiding it would break the resume.
90		// See server/githttp's gitsyncScaffoldPrefix, which pins the same literal for
91		// the writer-scope gate.
92		GitSyncScaffoldPrefix = "refs/gitsync/"
93	
94		// EntireCheckpointsPrefix is the checkpoint sub-namespace of refs/entire. It
95		// is the exception to the refs/entire rules: checkpoints are client-visible
96		// (un-hidden), user-amendable (pushable), and therefore recorded, while the
97		// rest of refs/entire stays hidden and reserved. refs/entire/checkpoints/* is
98		// written both by the entire-api path (repoapi commit_create) and by users.
99		EntireCheckpointsPrefix = "refs/entire/checkpoints"
100	
101		// EntirePoliciesPrefix is the checkpoint-policy sub-namespace of
102		// refs/entire. The entire CLI owns it: checkpointpolicy.Push writes
103		// refs/entire/policies/checkpoint, and the same package lists and fetches
104		// that ref to compare a local policy against the remote baseline.
105		//
106		// It therefore follows the EntireCheckpointsPrefix rules. The CLI is an
107		// ordinary client, so the ref is pushable by every caller, and it is
108		// advertised: a hidden ref returns nothing to the CLI's ls-remote and
109		// fails its fetch. It is not a branch, tag, or checkpoint, so no coverage
110		// mode signs it.
111		//
112		// Reserving this namespace refused two writers at once (ENT-2479): the
113		// CLI's own push, and the mirror worker's GitHub sync, which replays the
114		// ref a CLI left on the upstream. A worker-only carve-out fixes the sync
115		// and leaves every CLI user refused, so the opening is not scoped to a
116		// workload.
117		//
118		// entiredb stores the content and interprets none of it. Nothing here
119		// reads policy.json. Giving this ref a meaning in entiredb is a separate
120		// change: the refs already in the fleet were written under no server-side
121		// rule, so that change needs a migration over them, validation at the
122		// write path, or both, before anything may trust their content.
123		EntirePoliciesPrefix = "refs/entire/policies"
124	
125		// entireHeadsAnchor, unmirroredAnchor and nativeAnchor are the directory
126		// anchors that protect the two mirror-only Entire-owned branch namespaces
127		// (refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/* and refs/heads/entire/native/*). They are
128		// reserved on GitHub-mirror repos only; a native repo may use them as
129		// ordinary branches.
130		entireHeadsAnchor = "refs/heads/entire"
131		unmirroredAnchor  = "refs/heads/entire/unmirrored"
132		nativeAnchor      = "refs/heads/entire/native"
133	)
134	
135	// Domain is the class of repository a ref policy applies to. Native repos and
136	// GitHub mirrors share a base policy and differ only in their deltas.
137	type Domain int
138	
139	const (
140		// DomainNative is an Entire-native repository.
141		DomainNative Domain = iota
142		// DomainGitHubMirror is a repository mirrored from GitHub.
143		DomainGitHubMirror
144	)
145	
146	// DomainForMirror maps the repo row's is_mirror flag onto a Domain, keeping the
147	// classification in one place without coupling this package to repostore.
148	func DomainForMirror(isMirror bool) Domain {
149		if isMirror {
150			return DomainGitHubMirror
151		}
152		return DomainNative
153	}
154	
155	// Caller is the request identity a policy needs. Workload is the mTLS workload
156	// identity (empty for a public client). TrustedReader marks a caller that must
157	// see every ref regardless of hideRefs, i.e. backup/restore capture, so a
158	// bundle stays complete. The server adapts its request principal onto this.
159	type Caller struct {
160		Workload      servicetoken.Workload
161		TrustedReader bool
162		// NativeReplication marks the mirror-worker push that replicates a native
163		// primary's refs into a native-mirror PLACEMENT. It is the one caller that
164		// may write gittuf's namespace (see the carve-out in baseRules), because
165		// that push republishes trust material the primary already signed rather
166		// than authoring any. The server sets it from the repos row and the request
167		// principal together, never from the request alone.
168		NativeReplication bool
169	}
170	
171	// PushCheck is the reserved-ref verdict for one ref and caller.
172	type PushCheck struct {
173		// Reserved reports whether the ref falls in a reserved namespace.
174		Reserved bool
175		// Bucket is the matched rule, a low-cardinality metric label; "" when not
176		// reserved.
177		Bucket string
178		// Allowed reports whether this caller may push the ref: true when the ref is
179		// not reserved, or a carve-out lifts the reservation for this caller.
180		Allowed bool
181	}
182	
183	// carveOut lifts the reserved-ref gate on a namespace for named workloads.
184	// nativeReplicationOnly narrows it further, to the native-mirror replication
185	// push alone: the workload identity says WHO is calling, and that flag says
186	// WHICH of its pushes qualifies. A carve-out needs both when the same workload
187	// also runs pushes that must stay blocked.
188	type carveOut struct {
189		prefix                string
190		writers               []servicetoken.Workload
191		nativeReplicationOnly bool
192	}
193	
194	// rules is one layer's contribution to a policy. Layers are merged (see
195	// resolve); every field is additive.
196	type rules struct {
197		reservedPrefixes []string // matched with a trailing slash (path prefix)
198		reservedExact    []string // matched whole
199		pushOpenPrefixes []string // sub-prefixes pushable for ALL callers despite a reserved parent
200		carveOuts        []carveOut
201		hidePatterns     []string // uploadpack.hideRefs syntax (hiderefs.IsHidden)
202	}
203	
204	// Policy is the resolved, immutable ref policy for one domain. Its zero value is
205	// not valid; obtain one from a Resolver.
206	type Policy struct {
207		r rules
208	}
209	
210	// baseRules are the fleet-wide invariants that apply to every repo, whatever its
211	// domain. Each entry below notes why it is reserved/hidden and whether it can be
212	// overridden. The two override mechanisms are distinct:
213	//
214	//   - Push reservations are lifted two ways: a workload carve-out (see
215	//     carveOuts) opens a namespace to a named workload, and a pushOpenPrefixes
216	//     entry opens a sub-namespace to every caller (e.g. refs/entire/checkpoints/*
217	//     inside reserved refs/entire). The domain layer can add but never remove a
218	//     base reservation (tighten-only).
219	//   - Hide patterns are overridable per-subtree by a "!"-prefixed exception,
220	//     since hiderefs matching is last-match-wins (see hidePatterns).
221	func baseRules() rules {
222		return rules{
223			// Reserved from client push, matched as a path prefix (trailing slash
224			// required). Overridable only by a workload carve-out where noted.
225			reservedPrefixes: []string{
226				// Git convention for server-internal refs; also hidden from fetch
227				// (hidePatterns). Blocking push closes the write side. No carve-out.
228				InternalPrefix + "/",
229				// Node-local refs that never leave the server; also hidden from fetch
230				// (hidePatterns) and excluded from recording. Blocking push closes the
231				// write side. No carve-out.
232				LocalPrefix + "/",
233				// entiredb-managed refs; also hidden from fetch and excluded from
234				// recording. Reserved from direct client push, EXCEPT the two
235				// sub-namespaces in pushOpenPrefixes below: checkpoints and
236				// policies, both of which the entire CLI writes. The remainder is
237				// written only through server-side paths (not receive-pack), so
238				// this gate does not block them. No carve-out.
239				EntirePrefix + "/",
240				// Git object-replacement: a ref here rewrites how every cloner sees an
241				// object, so push is object substitution against all clients. No carve-out.
242				"refs/replace/",
243				// git bisect's session-local refs; meaningless on the server. No carve-out.
244				"refs/bisect/",
245				// The client's own remote-tracking view; no server-side meaning. No carve-out.
246				"refs/remotes/",
247				// Entire's structured-metadata namespace (ENT-1106), reserved so writes
248				// funnel through the git-meta service, which owns format + authz.
249				// OVERRIDABLE: the entire-api carve-out below lifts it for nested refs.
250				ManagedMetaPrefix,
251				// Git's GIT_NAMESPACE feature; entiredb uses one repo per ULID and never
252				// namespaces, so a push here makes double-nested refs no tool expects.
253				// No carve-out.
254				"refs/namespaces/",
255				// Prefix-form custom stash layouts (the bare refs/stash is an anchor
256				// below). No carve-out.
257				"refs/stash/",
258				// gittuf's namespace: the RSL is server-managed and user-authored
259				// policy/RSL is not supported yet, so the whole namespace is closed to
260				// direct client push. refs/gittuf/policy stays fetch-visible for
261				// verification. The server's own RSL writes bypass this gate.
262				// OVERRIDABLE: the native-replication carve-out below lifts it for the
263				// mirror worker replicating a primary into a native mirror.
264				GittufPrefix,
265			},
266			// Directory anchors: the bare namespace roots, reserved exact so a leaf ref
267			// squatting one cannot D/F-conflict with (and thereby block) every ref
268			// beneath it. Reserved for EVERY caller, carve-out workloads included: a
269			// carve-out matches by prefix + "/", so it never reaches the bare anchor,
270			// and the anchor's only legitimate writers create nested refs. Not
271			// overridable. refs/heads and refs/tags matter most on an uninitialised
272			// repo, where nothing beneath them exists yet to reject the squat; ordinary
273			// refs/heads/* and refs/tags/* stay pushable.
274			reservedExact: []string{
275				"refs/heads", // blocks squatting the branch root
276				"refs/tags",  // blocks squatting the tag root
277				"refs/stash",
278				"refs/meta",
279				"refs/meta/entire",
280				"refs/gittuf",
281				EntirePrefix,            // refs/entire anchor, matching its reserved prefix above
282				EntireCheckpointsPrefix, // refs/entire/checkpoints anchor, so squatting the bare leaf can't block the pushable checkpoints/* subtree
283				EntirePoliciesPrefix,    // refs/entire/policies anchor, for the same reason as checkpoints above
284			},
285			// Pushable for ALL callers despite the reserved refs/entire/ parent: the
286			// entire CLI writes both sub-namespaces as an ordinary client, so a
287			// workload carve-out cannot express either one. Nested refs only; both
288			// bare anchors stay reserved (above). Both are un-hidden below, so
289			// recording follows the push opening rather than trailing it.
290			pushOpenPrefixes: []string{
291				EntireCheckpointsPrefix + "/",
292				EntirePoliciesPrefix + "/",
293			},
294			// Carve-outs are the ONLY way to lift a push reservation: each names the
295			// workload(s) allowed to write an otherwise-reserved namespace, matched by
296			// prefix + "/" (so the bare directory anchor stays reserved even for them).
297			carveOuts: []carveOut{
298				// entire-api owns refs/meta/entire/* (nested refs only).
299				{prefix: ManagedMetaPrefix, writers: []servicetoken.Workload{servicetoken.WorkloadEntireAPI}},
300				// The mirror worker replicates a native primary's refs/gittuf/** into a
301				// native-mirror placement (ENT-2423). Without this the bootstrap push
302				// carries the primary's policy and RSL, the whole push is refused, and
303				// the mirror can never hold managed refs — which is the very condition
304				// that selects bootstrap, so it never converges.
305				//
306				// The carve-out admits the push; it does not trust it. The mirror is a
307				// read-only copy, so what lands must be exactly what the primary
308				// published: refstore's fast-forward guard refuses a rewind of the
309				// namespace, the rooted-policy pin refuses a forward swap to a different
310				// root, and recording is suppressed under this mode so the placement
311				// never signs an entry of its own.
312				//
313				// The worker's GitHub-mirror syncs carry the same workload identity and
314				// are NOT covered: nativeReplicationOnly keys on the target being a
315				// native-mirror placement, so a GitHub mirror's trust material stays
316				// closed until ENT-1395 decides what it should be.
317				{
318					prefix:                GittufPrefix,
319					writers:               []servicetoken.Workload{servicetoken.WorkloadMirrorWorker},
320					nativeReplicationOnly: true,
321				},
322			},
323			// Hidden from external fetch: the entiredb-internal namespaces only. The
324			// RSL and policy-staging are deliberately NOT hidden (gittuf clients fetch
325			// the RSL to verify); they are carved out of recording instead, see
326			// ShouldRecord.
327			//
328			// OVERRIDABLE per subtree: hiderefs matching is last-match-wins, so a
329			// "!"-prefixed pattern appended AFTER a hide un-hides that subtree. The two
330			// exceptions below are exactly that: refs/entire is hidden, then each
331			// "!" pattern advertises one sub-namespace as a visible island inside the
332			// otherwise-hidden refs/entire. Of the two, only checkpoints are inside
333			// a coverage mode, so only checkpoint updates are signed.
334			//
335			// Both islands exist because the entire CLI reads them over the wire. It
336			// is an ordinary client, so hiding a ref does not merely conceal it: the
337			// CLI's ls-remote returns nothing and its fetch fails.
338			hidePatterns: []string{
339				InternalPrefix,                // server-internal refs (synthetic haves, etc.)
340				LocalPrefix,                   // node-local refs that never leave the server
341				EntirePrefix,                  // entiredb-managed refs (future trust material, etc.)
342				"!" + EntireCheckpointsPrefix, // un-hide checkpoints (must follow EntirePrefix)
343				"!" + EntirePoliciesPrefix,    // un-hide checkpoint policy (must follow EntirePrefix)
344			},
345		}
346	}
347	
348	// domainRules are the per-domain deltas layered onto baseRules. A delta is
349	// tighten-only: it adds reservations/hides, never removes a base one. Only the
350	// GitHub-mirror domain adds rules today.
351	func domainRules(d Domain) rules {
352		if d == DomainGitHubMirror {
353			// Mirror-only: these anchors protect two mirror features and would
354			// D/F-conflict with refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/* and
355			// refs/heads/entire/native/*. Reserved exact, so not overridable by a
356			// carve-out (as with the base anchors). Native repos omit them, so all
357			// three stay ordinary branches there.
358			return rules{reservedExact: []string{entireHeadsAnchor, unmirroredAnchor, nativeAnchor}}
359		}
360		return rules{}
361	}
362	
363	// Resolver hands out the resolved Policy for a domain. It is the seam the git
364	// server and the recording store depend on, so neither hardcodes ref lists and
365	// the three consumers cannot drift.
366	type Resolver interface {
367		For(d Domain) Policy
368	}
369	
370	type resolver struct{}
371	
372	// NewResolver returns the default resolver over the built-in base and domain
373	// rules.
374	func NewResolver() Resolver { return resolver{} }
375	
376	func (resolver) For(d Domain) Policy { return Policy{r: resolve(d)} }
377	
378	// resolve merges the base layer with the domain delta. Merge is union: each
379	// layer only adds, so a lower layer can tighten but never loosen a base
380	// invariant.
381	func resolve(d Domain) rules {
382		base := baseRules()
383		delta := domainRules(d)
384		return rules{
385			reservedPrefixes: append(base.reservedPrefixes, delta.reservedPrefixes...),
386			reservedExact:    append(base.reservedExact, delta.reservedExact...),
387			pushOpenPrefixes: append(base.pushOpenPrefixes, delta.pushOpenPrefixes...),
388			carveOuts:        append(base.carveOuts, delta.carveOuts...),
389			hidePatterns:     append(base.hidePatterns, delta.hidePatterns...),
390		}
391	}
392	
393	// CheckPush reports whether caller may push ref under this policy.
394	func (p Policy) CheckPush(ref string, caller Caller) PushCheck {
395		bucket := p.reservedBucket(ref)
396		if bucket == "" {
397			return PushCheck{Reserved: false, Allowed: true}
398		}
399		return PushCheck{Reserved: true, Bucket: bucket, Allowed: p.carvedOut(ref, caller)}
400	}
401	
402	// reservedBucket returns the reserved rule ref matched: the exact ref for an
403	// exact hit, otherwise the matched prefix, and "" when nothing matches. The
404	// return value doubles as a bounded metric label.
405	//
406	// Order matters: exact anchors are checked first (so a bare directory anchor
407	// stays reserved), then the pushOpenPrefixes exceptions (a sub-namespace made
408	// pushable inside a reserved parent, e.g. refs/entire/checkpoints/*), then the
409	// reserved prefixes. A ref under an open exception is not reserved.
410	func (p Policy) reservedBucket(ref string) string {
411		for _, exact := range p.r.reservedExact {
412			if ref == exact {
413				return exact
414			}
415		}
416		for _, open := range p.r.pushOpenPrefixes {
417			if strings.HasPrefix(ref, open) {
418				return ""
419			}
420		}
421		for _, prefix := range p.r.reservedPrefixes {
422			if strings.HasPrefix(ref, prefix) {
423				return prefix
424			}
425		}
426		return ""
427	}
428	
429	// carvedOut reports whether a carve-out lifts the reservation of ref for caller.
430	// An empty workload never matches, so a public client is never carved out. A
431	// carve-out marked nativeReplicationOnly also needs the caller to be the
432	// native-mirror replication push.
433	func (p Policy) carvedOut(ref string, caller Caller) bool {
434		if caller.Workload == "" {
435			return false
436		}
437		for _, co := range p.r.carveOuts {
438			if co.nativeReplicationOnly && !caller.NativeReplication {
439				continue
440			}
441			if strings.HasPrefix(ref, co.prefix) && slices.Contains(co.writers, caller.Workload) {
442				return true
443			}
444		}
445		return false
446	}
447	
448	// Hidden reports whether ref is hidden from an external client's advertisement.
449	// It is caller-independent: the trusted-reader exemption is applied by
450	// HideRefsFor, not here, so Hidden also serves as the recording basis.
451	func (p Policy) Hidden(ref string) bool {
452		return hiderefs.IsHidden(p.r.hidePatterns, ref)
453	}
454	
455	// InGittufNamespace reports whether ref is part of gittuf's reserved namespace
456	// (refs/gittuf/**), which holds the RSL, the root-of-trust policy, and gittuf's
457	// staging and attestation refs. It is a pure predicate on the ref name, caller-
458	// and domain-independent, so every server ref-write path can use one definition
459	// of "this is trust material" rather than re-deriving the prefix. The
460	// fast-forward-only invariant on this namespace (a rewrite of a signed trust ref
461	// is a rollback attack, never a legitimate ordinary write) keys on this.
462	func InGittufNamespace(ref string) bool {
463		return strings.HasPrefix(ref, GittufPrefix)
464	}
465	
466	// ShouldRecord reports whether a push to ref should produce a signed RSL entry.
467	// A ref is recorded iff it is visible to an external client, minus the
468	// carve-outs that are visible but must not be logged:
469	//
470	//   - the RSL itself (logging the log is recursive) and the staging policy;
471	//   - unmirrored branches (refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/*): these stay advertised
472	//     on fetch (see the unmirrored-branches ADR) but live only in Entire and are
473	//     never mirrored to GitHub, so they are outside the attested history and must
474	//     not be signed; and
475	//   - git-sync's transfer scaffolding (refs/gitsync/**): a replication target
476	//     writes it during a batched bootstrap and deletes it again, and the primary
477	//     never holds one, so no entry for it can exist to attest.
478	//
479	// Both name-keyed carve-outs are unconditional (all domains), so recording is
480	// stricter than fetch visibility for these two subtrees. Neither is simply added
481	// to the fetch hide set: the ADR keeps unmirrored branches visible on
482	// clone/fetch, and git-sync reads its own scaffolding back to resume a bootstrap.
483	//
484	// This predicate is also what the placement acceptance verifier admits refs by,
485	// so a ref recorded here must be one the primary's RSL can attest. A visible ref
486	// with no possible entry — scaffolding is exactly that — fails acceptance on a
487	// correctly converged placement unless it is carved out here.
488	func (p Policy) ShouldRecord(ref string) bool {
489		return p.RecordSkipReason(ref) == RecordSkipNone
490	}
491	
492	// RecordSkip categorizes why RecordSkipReason excluded a ref from RSL
493	// recording. The values are bounded telemetry labels; RecordSkipNone means the
494	// ref is recorded.
495	type RecordSkip string
496	
497	const (
498		RecordSkipNone       RecordSkip = ""
499		RecordSkipHidden     RecordSkip = "hidden"
500		RecordSkipReserved   RecordSkip = "reserved"
501		RecordSkipUnmirrored RecordSkip = "unmirrored"
502		// RecordSkipScaffold: git-sync's target-local transfer scaffolding
503		// (refs/gitsync/**). Visible like an unmirrored branch, and excluded for the
504		// same kind of reason: it is not repository content and the primary never
505		// holds it, so it is outside the attested history.
506		RecordSkipScaffold RecordSkip = "scaffold"
507		// RecordSkipOutsideCoverage: the ref is recordable in principle but sits
508		// outside this repo's RSL coverage mode (ADR 20260905 section 2.3). Unlike
509		// the other three, this reason is per repo, not per ref name.
510		RecordSkipOutsideCoverage RecordSkip = "outside_coverage"
511	)
512	
513	// RecordSkipReason classifies ref against the recording carve-outs documented
514	// on ShouldRecord: hidden (not client-visible), reserved (the RSL itself and
515	// the staging policy), unmirrored (refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/*), or scaffold
516	// (refs/gitsync/**).
517	// ShouldRecord is defined as this returning RecordSkipNone, so the
518	// classification cannot drift from the predicate.
519	func (p Policy) RecordSkipReason(ref string) RecordSkip {
520		switch {
521		case p.Hidden(ref):
522			return RecordSkipHidden
523		case ref == RSLRef || ref == PolicyStagingRef:
524			return RecordSkipReserved
525		case isUnmirrored(ref):
526			return RecordSkipUnmirrored
527		case strings.HasPrefix(ref, GitSyncScaffoldPrefix):
528			return RecordSkipScaffold
529		default:
530			return RecordSkipNone
531		}
532	}
533	
534	// isUnmirrored reports whether ref is an unmirrored branch
535	// (refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/*). The trailing slash is the namespace
536	// boundary: refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/x matches, refs/heads/entire/unmirroredish
537	// does not, and the bare anchor refs/heads/entire/unmirrored is not itself
538	// unmirrored. This matches mirror.IsUnmirroredRef by convention. refpolicy is a
539	// foundational package and does not depend on the heavier mirror package, so the
540	// prefix is derived from the local unmirroredAnchor constant rather than shared
541	// as a symbol. The unmirrored-branches ADR pins the literal against drift.
542	func isUnmirrored(ref string) bool {
543		return strings.HasPrefix(ref, unmirroredAnchor+"/")
544	}
545	
546	// HideRefsFor returns the uploadpack.hideRefs patterns to apply for caller. A
547	// trusted reader (backup/restore capture) is exempt and sees every ref, so a
548	// bundle it builds stays complete; every other caller gets the domain hide set.
549	func (p Policy) HideRefsFor(caller Caller) []string {
550		if caller.TrustedReader {
551			return nil
552		}
553		return p.r.hidePatterns
554	}
555

19		"entire.io/slogutil"

22	const (
23		// SyncKindHeader declares which mirror-worker job kind a sync push
24		// belongs to. Only the namespace kind may write the Entire-owned
25		// namespace; see namespaceWriterScopeErrors.
26		SyncKindHeader = "X-Entire-Sync-Kind"
27	
28		// SyncKindNamespace is the mirror-worker source kind that replicates
29		// mirror.NativeRefPrefix. It matches the NATS source kind mirror-pipeline
30		// publishes namespace jobs under, so the two must change together.
31		SyncKindNamespace = "entiredb_ns"
32	
33		// gitsyncScaffoldPrefix is git-sync's own temp-ref namespace on a sync
34		// TARGET: a batched bootstrap parks each branch at
35		// refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch> and removes it when the branch
36		// lands. Scaffolding, not content — the sync creates and deletes these
37		// itself. refpolicy reserves no part of it, so every other caller may
38		// already write it; it does carve the namespace out of RSL recording, since
39		// a target-only ref has no entry on the primary to attest.
40		gitsyncScaffoldPrefix = refpolicy.GitSyncScaffoldPrefix
41	)
42	
43	// errNamespaceWriterScope is the per-ref refusal a worker sync gets for the
44	// Entire-owned namespace. The worker's job kind, not the ref, is what is
45	// wrong, so the text names the kind.
46	var errNamespaceWriterScope = errors.New(
47		"mirror-worker syncs may not write refs/heads/entire/native/*; declare " +
48			SyncKindHeader + ": " + SyncKindNamespace)
49	
50	// namespaceWriterScopeErrors holds a mirror-worker sync to the ref scope its
51	// declared job kind owns, refusing every command outside it.
52	//
53	// This is the server half of the two-writer split a GitHub mirror gets once
54	// the namespace ships: the GitHub-kind sync owns every ordinary ref, the
55	// namespace-kind sync owns refs/heads/entire/native/*, and neither may touch
56	// the other's refs. Both directions are enforced, keyed on the sync-kind
57	// header:
58	//
59	//   - A sync declaring SyncKindNamespace may write ONLY refs the namespace
60	//     routes (routesWithNamespace), plus git-sync's own scaffolding under
61	//     gitsyncScaffoldPrefix. Every other command in that push is refused.
62	//     The namespace job's scope IS the namespace, so this cannot refuse a
63	//     legitimate write.
64	//   - A sync declaring nothing — the GitHub-kind sync — may write everything
65	//     EXCEPT those refs.
66	//
67	// The worker also carries a ref-exclusion list, but that list is only as safe
68	// as the oldest worker build allowed to run — rolling the GitHub worker back
69	// to a build without it would restore a destructive prune of the whole
70	// namespace. Enforcing the scope here makes the exclusion an optimisation
71	// that avoids noisy refusals, not the safety property. The reverse direction
72	// is the same argument pointed the other way: a namespace worker that lost
73	// its scope must not be able to prune the refs GitHub owns.
74	//
75	// Refusals are per ref so the rest of a sync still converges: an obsolete
76	// GitHub worker's prune of the namespace is dropped and its ordinary refs
77	// land. Deletes are refused like creates and updates — a prune IS the
78	// dangerous case.
79	//
80	// Only ref commands are in scope. HEAD moves through RepoAdmin.SetDefaultBranch
81	// as a symref, never as a receive-pack command, so the default-branch
82	// reconcile is unaffected by either rule.
83	//
84	// A sync that declares nothing is gated on GITHUB-MIRROR ROWS ONLY. On every
85	// other row the namespace is not Entire-owned: refpolicy reserves the anchor
86	// on the GitHub-mirror domain alone, so refs/heads/entire/native/* is an
87	// ordinary branch on a native repo. Its placements are replicated by the
88	// entiredb-kind sync, which declares no kind and is the sole writer at every
89	// replica — scoping the undeclared direction to mirror rows is what keeps
90	// that sync from refusing those branches forever.
91	//
92	// A sync that DECLARES the namespace kind is held to the namespace on every
93	// row class. It is a claim about the job, not about the row, and the row
94	// class it writes today is not a reason to let a mis-targeted job prune a
95	// native replica whole.
96	//
97	// workerPush is derived from the request principal rather than passed in
98	// because every caller of HandleReceivePack must be covered: a caller that
99	// forgot the argument would silently disable the scope. mirrorRepo IS a
100	// parameter because it is a property of the repos row, which this function
101	// does not load.
102	func namespaceWriterScopeErrors(
103		ctx context.Context,
104		r *http.Request,
105		mirrorRepo bool,
106		repoID string,
107		commands []*packp.Command,
108	) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error {
109		principal, _ := reqctx.GetPrincipal(ctx)
110		if !isMirrorWorker(principal) {
111			return nil
112		}
113		declaredKind := r.Header.Get(SyncKindHeader)
114		namespaceSync := declaredKind == SyncKindNamespace
115		if !mirrorRepo && !namespaceSync {
116			return nil
117		}
118		var refused map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error
119		for _, command := range commands {
120			// A command is in scope when the ref's side of the split matches the
121			// writer's. The two rules are one comparison because they are one
122			// rule: each writer owns exactly one side.
123			//
124			// forge.NamespaceOwned, not IsNativeNamespaceRef: the bare anchor
125			// sits on the namespace's side of the split, because a write to it
126			// decides the fate of every ref inside. It takes the row class
127			// because a worker sync resolves no routing at all.
128			//
129			// refpolicy also reserves the anchor exactly on the GitHub-mirror
130			// domain, and that check runs before this one and refuses the whole
131			// request, so today the anchor never reaches here. This gate does not
132			// rely on that: the two answer to different owners (a reserved name
133			// versus a declared writer), and a later carve-out or reordering must
134			// not silently open the anchor to a worker sync.
135			//
136			// The declared kind is ORed into the row class so a namespace sync is
137			// scoped to the namespace on a native row too, where the namespace is
138			// an ordinary branch that this row class does not own.
139			// git-sync parks a batched bootstrap's branches under
140			// gitsyncScaffoldPrefix on the target, so the FIRST namespace sync
141			// onto a replica that holds none of these refs writes them. That push
142			// is the one that cannot be retried into success, and the header-less
143			// GitHub-kind sync writes the same scaffolding already: admitting it
144			// here makes the two writers symmetric on their own temp refs, and
145			// reaches no content ref either of them owns. The trailing slash
146			// keeps the bare anchor out, as everywhere else.
147			if namespaceSync && strings.HasPrefix(command.Name.String(), gitsyncScaffoldPrefix) {
148				continue
149			}
150			if forge.NamespaceOwned(mirrorRepo || namespaceSync, command.Name) == namespaceSync {
151				continue
152			}
153			if refused == nil {
154				refused = make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error, 1)
155			}
156			if namespaceSync {
157				refused[command.Name] = fmt.Errorf(
158					"namespace sync may not write %s; it is scoped to %s*", command.Name, mirror.NativeRefPrefix)
159			} else {
160				refused[command.Name] = errNamespaceWriterScope
161			}
162			slogutil.Warn(ctx, "receive-pack: refusing worker sync write outside its ref scope",
163				slog.String("repo_id", repoID),
164				slog.String("ref", command.Name.String()),
165				slog.String("declared_sync_kind", declaredKind))
166			secsignal.Emit(ctx, secsignal.PushRejected,
167				secsignal.WithSurface("githttp"),
168				secsignal.WithReason(scopeSignalReason(namespaceSync)),
169				secsignal.WithResource("repo", repoID),
170				secsignal.WithDetail("security.detail.ref", command.Name.String()))
171		}
172		return refused
173	}

175	// scopeSignalReason separates the two directions in the security signal, so a
176	// namespace worker reaching outside its scope is not indistinguishable from
177	// an obsolete GitHub worker pruning the namespace.
178	func scopeSignalReason(namespaceSync bool) string {
179		if namespaceSync {
180			return "namespace_sync_out_of_scope"
181		}
182		return "worker_namespace_scope"
183	}

370			//

413							slog.String("repo_id", repoID.String()))

415						return

419				// ClearMirrorUpstream has turned the row native (ENT-2726). The
420				// detached_at stamp makes that definitive, so it is routine too.
421				if repoRowFound && !repoRow.DetachedAt.IsZero() {
422					slogutil.Info(ctx, "write-mirror push to detached repo rejected",
423						slog.String("repo_id", repoID.String()),
424						slog.Time("detached_at", repoRow.DetachedAt))
425					http.Error(w, "repository was detached from GitHub", http.StatusForbidden)
426					return

50	// namespaceWriterScopeErrors holds a mirror-worker sync to the ref scope its
51	// declared job kind owns, refusing every command outside it.
52	//
53	// This is the server half of the two-writer split a GitHub mirror gets once
54	// the namespace ships: the GitHub-kind sync owns every ordinary ref, the
55	// namespace-kind sync owns refs/heads/entire/native/*, and neither may touch
56	// the other's refs. Both directions are enforced, keyed on the sync-kind

62	//     The namespace job's scope IS the namespace, so this cannot refuse a
63	//     legitimate write.
64	//   - A sync declaring nothing — the GitHub-kind sync — may write everything
65	//     EXCEPT those refs.

73	// its scope must not be able to prune the refs GitHub owns.

102	func namespaceWriterScopeErrors(
103		ctx context.Context,
104		r *http.Request,
105		mirrorRepo bool,
106		repoID string,
107		commands []*packp.Command,
108	) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]error {
109		principal, _ := reqctx.GetPrincipal(ctx)
110		if !isMirrorWorker(principal) {
111			return nil
112		}

116			return nil
117		}

119		for _, command := range commands {

121			// writer's. The two rules are one comparison because they are one
122			// rule: each writer owns exactly one side.
123			//

125			// sits on the namespace's side of the split, because a write to it

135			//

140			// gitsyncScaffoldPrefix on the target, so the FIRST namespace sync
141			// onto a replica that holds none of these refs writes them. That push
142			// is the one that cannot be retried into success, and the header-less
143			// GitHub-kind sync writes the same scaffolding already: admitting it
144			// here makes the two writers symmetric on their own temp refs, and
145			// reaches no content ref either of them owns. The trailing slash
146			// keeps the bare anchor out, as everywhere else.
147			if namespaceSync && strings.HasPrefix(command.Name.String(), gitsyncScaffoldPrefix) {

149			}

168				secsignal.WithReason(scopeSignalReason(namespaceSync)),
169				secsignal.WithResource("repo", repoID),
170				secsignal.WithDetail("security.detail.ref", command.Name.String()))
171		}

173	}

14	// PlacementCompletionWriter is the native-mirror half of the composite
15	// writer: nativemirror.Service's intent-aware ApplyCompletionStatus,
16	// which honors a completion only for a serving-eligible, active,
17	// unsuspended placement whose creation has not permanently failed, and
18	// reports whether a row actually changed. sourcePosition is the worker's
19	// pre-fetch snapshot of the primary's write position; a ready completion
20	// advances the placement's applied watermark to at least it (0 stamps
21	// nothing).
22	type PlacementCompletionWriter interface {
23		ApplyCompletionStatus(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID, status string, sourcePosition int64) (bool, error)
24	}

26	// StatusWriter is the mirror_repos.status surface of the composite writer's
27	// GitHub-mirror leg. *mirrorrepo.Service satisfies it. Both methods are
28	// best-effort and idempotent: a no-op (deleted/suspended/already-terminal
29	// row) returns nil so the message is Acked, not retried.
30	type StatusWriter interface {
31		MarkReady(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID) error
32		MarkFailed(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID) error
33	}

42	// CompositeStatusWriter fans one repo_ops_v1 done-event to both status
43	// stores: mirror_repos (GitHub mirrors) and native_mirrors (native-mirror
44	// placements). The two ULID spaces are disjoint and neither store can
45	// tell "not mine" from "mine but nothing to do" (both writers are
46	// best-effort no-ops on a miss — the mirror writer surfaces no
47	// ErrNotFound to chain on), so every completion is applied to both and
48	// at most one row changes.
49	//
50	// Both legs run on every completion — a failure in one never skips the
51	// other — and their errors are joined: any error Naks the message and
52	// both legs re-run on redelivery, which is safe because each is
53	// idempotent. The status strings are shared vocabulary: this package's
54	// StatusReady/StatusFailed match mirrorrepo's and nativemirror's.
55	type CompositeStatusWriter struct {
56		// Mirrors drives mirror_repos.status (*mirrorrepo.Service).
57		Mirrors StatusWriter
58		// NativeMirrors drives native_mirrors.status (*nativemirror.Service).
59		NativeMirrors PlacementCompletionWriter
60	}

62	// CompositeMarkStore is the InitialSyncMarkStore over both placement tables.
63	// Mirrors is *mirrorrepo.Service and NativeMirrors is *nativemirror.Service.
64	// The ULID spaces are disjoint, so exactly one leg owns a given id.
65	type CompositeMarkStore struct {
66		Mirrors       InitialSyncMarkStore
67		NativeMirrors InitialSyncMarkStore
68	}

70	// InitialSyncMarked reports whether either placement table records the flag
71	// as landed. The composite reads the other leg before it returns a leg
72	// error, so a healthy true still short-circuits the marker.
73	func (c CompositeMarkStore) InitialSyncMarked(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID) (bool, error) {
74		var errs []error
75		for _, leg := range []InitialSyncMarkStore{c.Mirrors, c.NativeMirrors} {
76			marked, err := leg.InitialSyncMarked(ctx, id)
77			if err != nil {
78				errs = append(errs, err)
79				continue
80			}
81			if marked {
82				return true, nil
83			}
84		}
85		return false, errors.Join(errs...)
86	}

88	// RecordInitialSyncMarked stamps whichever placement table owns the row. Both
89	// legs run; the one that does not own the ULID is a no-op.
90	func (c CompositeMarkStore) RecordInitialSyncMarked(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID) error {
91		return errors.Join(
92			c.Mirrors.RecordInitialSyncMarked(ctx, id),
93			c.NativeMirrors.RecordInitialSyncMarked(ctx, id),
94		)
95	}

97	func (c CompositeStatusWriter) ApplyCompletion(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID, status string, sourcePosition int64) error {
98		var mirrorErr error
99		mirrorStart := time.Now()
100		switch status {
101		case StatusReady:
102			mirrorErr = c.Mirrors.MarkReady(ctx, id)
103		case StatusFailed:
104			mirrorErr = c.Mirrors.MarkFailed(ctx, id)
105		default:
106			// decodeEvent has already rejected unknown statuses; defensive.
107			return fmt.Errorf("unknown completion status %q", status)
108		}
109		recordLegDuration(ctx, mirrorStart, legMirrorStatus, mirrorErr)
110		if mirrorErr != nil {
111			mirrorErr = fmt.Errorf("mirror status write: %w", mirrorErr)
112		}
113	
114		nativeStart := time.Now()
115		applied, nativeErr := c.NativeMirrors.ApplyCompletionStatus(ctx, id, status, sourcePosition)
116		recordLegDuration(ctx, nativeStart, legNativeStatus, nativeErr)
117		if nativeErr != nil {
118			nativeErr = fmt.Errorf("native-mirror status write: %w", nativeErr)
119		}
120		if applied {
121			// The consumer's "mirror-done applied" line fires for every ack;
122			// this one fires only when a native_mirrors row actually changed,
123			// so completions the intent gate silently drops stay
124			// distinguishable from ones that landed.
125			//
126			// NOTE: since the applied watermark landed, "changed" means EITHER a
127			// status transition OR a watermark-only advance, and the two are not
128			// distinguishable from here — the store reports one bool. That makes
129			// this line once-per-push-per-placement in steady state rather than
130			// roughly once per placement lifetime, and it is no longer a reliable
131			// marker of processing->ready specifically. Use the status column for
132			// transitions; treat this as sync progress.
133			slogutil.Info(ctx, "native-mirror completion applied",
134				slog.String("placement_id", id.String()),
135				slog.String("status", status),
136				slog.Int64("source_position", sourcePosition),
137			)
138		}
139	
140		return errors.Join(mirrorErr, nativeErr)
141	}

607	// with AdvanceStage's fenced CAS (which requires suspended_at IS NULL): every
608	// suspended row today is also desired_state='deleted' (MarkDesiredDeleted
609	// sets both) so it is reaped via the deleted leg, but without this guard a

612	// spin the drain loop.

614	// any executor may reclaim (attempts bumps again — the retry counter
615	// counts real executions, capping is the caller's policy).

628			 WHERE id = (
629			     SELECT nr.id
630			     FROM native_mirrors nr
631			     JOIN clusters c ON c.slug = nr.cluster_slug
632			     WHERE c.jurisdiction = $2
633			       AND (nr.claimed_at IS NULL
634			            OR nr.claimed_at < now() - ($3::INT8 * INTERVAL '1 microsecond'))
635			       AND (nr.next_retry_at IS NULL OR nr.next_retry_at <= now())
636			       AND (nr.desired_state = 'deleted'
637			            OR (nr.desired_state = 'active'
638			                AND nr.stage <> 'announced'
639			                AND nr.creation_failed_at IS NULL
640			                AND nr.suspended_at IS NULL
641			                AND c.decommissioned_at IS NULL))

656	// AdvanceStage is the fenced stage CAS: it moves id from → to only while
657	// the caller still holds the claim, the row is not marked for deletion, and
658	// it is not suspended. Returns false without error when the guard fails —
659	// the caller re-reads and decides (deletion intended → teardown leg;
660	// otherwise another executor won and this one walks away).
661	//
662	// A successful transition also clears last_error: forward progress means the
663	// transient failure that RecordRetry last recorded is resolved, so a healthy
664	// placement (e.g. one that reaches announced after an earlier retry) doesn't
665	// keep stale failure text.
666	func (s *Service) AdvanceStage(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID, claimedBy, from, to string) (bool, error) {
667		tag, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx,
668			`UPDATE native_mirrors
669			 SET stage = $4, stage_updated_at = now(), last_error = ''
670			 WHERE id = $1 AND claimed_by = $2 AND stage = $3
671			   AND desired_state = 'active' AND suspended_at IS NULL`,
672			id, claimedBy, from, to)
673		if err != nil {
674			return false, fmt.Errorf("nativemirror: advance %s %s→%s: %w", id, from, to, err)
675		}
676		return tag.RowsAffected() > 0, nil
677	}

679	// CreatedEvent is the fully marshaled native_mirror.created message Announce
680	// durably enqueues alongside the terminal stage CAS. The executor builds it
681	// with resourceevents.NewMessage while it has the mirror meta and primaries in
682	// hand; the relay republishes the stored bytes verbatim, so nothing is
683	// re-derived at publish time. MsgID is the JetStream deduplication key
684	// ("native_mirror.created/<repo_id>").
685	type CreatedEvent struct {
686		MsgID   string
687		Subject string
688		Payload []byte
689	}

691	// Announce is the seeded→announced arm of AdvanceStage fused with the durable
692	// enqueue of the placement's native_mirror.created event: one transaction runs
693	// the fenced stage CAS (same guard as AdvanceStage, including the last_error
694	// clear) and inserts the outbox row, so the event is queued iff the placement
695	// actually announced. The relay (CreatedOutboxRelay) publishes it with PubAck
696	// and deletes the row only after the ack — a crash anywhere between this
697	// commit and the publish re-delivers, and the stream's msg-id dedup plus the
698	// consumer's idempotence absorb duplicates. Returns false without error when
699	// the guard fails, exactly like AdvanceStage.
700	//
701	// CockroachDB can abort the commit with SQLSTATE 40001 even without a
702	// competing writer: the outbox INSERT is a pipelined write, and a lease
703	// transfer or range split under it surfaces at COMMIT as
704	// RETRY_ASYNC_WRITE_FAILURE. Nothing is committed, so the transaction
705	// replays like Register instead of costing the placement an executor
706	// backoff.
707	func (s *Service) Announce(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID, claimedBy, jurisdiction string, ev CreatedEvent) (bool, error) {
708		if ev.MsgID == "" || ev.Subject == "" || len(ev.Payload) == 0 || jurisdiction == "" {
709			return false, errors.New("nativemirror: announce requires a jurisdiction and a fully built created event")
710		}
711		return retryOnSerializationFailure(ctx, "announce "+id.String(), func() (bool, error) {
712			return s.announceTx(ctx, id, claimedBy, jurisdiction, ev)
713		})
714	}

716	func (s *Service) announceTx(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID, claimedBy, jurisdiction string, ev CreatedEvent) (bool, error) {
717		tx, err := s.pool.Begin(ctx)
718		if err != nil {
719			return false, fmt.Errorf("nativemirror: begin announce %s: %w", id, err)
720		}
721		defer tx.Rollback(ctx) //nolint:errcheck // no-op after commit
722		tag, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
723			`UPDATE native_mirrors
724			 SET stage = $3, stage_updated_at = now(), last_error = ''
725			 WHERE id = $1 AND claimed_by = $2 AND stage = $4
726			   AND desired_state = 'active' AND suspended_at IS NULL`,
727			id, claimedBy, StageAnnounced, StageSeeded)
728		if err != nil {
729			return false, fmt.Errorf("nativemirror: announce %s: %w", id, err)
730		}
731		if tag.RowsAffected() == 0 {
732			return false, nil
733		}
734		// Plain INSERT, deliberately no ON CONFLICT: the fenced CAS above fires at
735		// most once per placement (announced rows are never re-claimed and
736		// ResetForRetry cannot reach an announced row), repo ULIDs are never
737		// reused, and teardown-vs-announce serializes through the native_mirrors
738		// row guard — so a conflicting row is an invariant break that must surface
739		// as an error, not be silently kept with a stale payload.
740		if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
741			`INSERT INTO `+createdOutboxTable+` (repo_id, subject, msg_id, payload, jurisdiction)
742			 VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)`,
743			id, ev.Subject, ev.MsgID, ev.Payload, jurisdiction); err != nil {
744			return false, fmt.Errorf("nativemirror: enqueue created event %s: %w", id, err)
745		}
746		if err := tx.Commit(ctx); err != nil {
747			return false, fmt.Errorf("nativemirror: commit announce %s: %w", id, err)
748		}
749		return true, nil
750	}

1232	// ApplyCompletionStatus applies a worker completion (ready/failed) to a
1233	// placement's SYNC status and, on ready, advances its applied write
1234	// watermark. It is the intent-aware half of the composite done-event writer:
1235	// a completion is honored only for a serving-eligible, active, unsuspended
1236	// placement whose creation has not permanently failed — a half-created,
1237	// deleting, or dead placement must never change state off a completion that
1238	// raced its lifecycle. Twin-parity semantics with mirrorrepo: 'ready' heals a
1239	// prior sync failure but never resurrects a permanent creation failure;
1240	// 'failed' applies only to a processing row (a retry-exhausted sync can never
1241	// regress a placement that has already gone ready). Best-effort and
1242	// idempotent: matching nothing returns applied=false with no error, and the
1243	// consumer acks either way.
1244	//
1245	// sourcePosition is the primary write-position ordinal the worker snapshotted
1246	// before fetching (ADR 20260818-native-mirror-resync-sweep); a converging
1247	// sync holds at least everything up to it, so 'ready' stamps
1248	// applied_position = GREATEST(applied_position, sourcePosition) — monotonic,
1249	// and conservative under redelivery or out-of-order completions. The ready
1250	// guard admits an already-ready row whose watermark would advance, so every
1251	// event-driven sync keeps the watermark current after the first ready; 0
1252	// (an old worker's omitted field) can never match that arm and degrades to
1253	// the pure status transition. A 'failed' completion proves nothing about
1254	// applied state and stamps nothing.
1255	func (s *Service) ApplyCompletionStatus(ctx context.Context, id model.RepoID, status string, sourcePosition int64) (bool, error) {
1256		if status != StatusReady && status != StatusFailed {
1257			return false, fmt.Errorf("nativemirror: invalid completion status %q", status)
1258		}
1259		if status == StatusFailed {
1260			tag, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx,
1261				`UPDATE native_mirrors
1262				 SET status = $2
1263				 WHERE id = $1 AND `+completionEligible+`
1264				   AND status = 'processing'`,
1265				id, status)
1266			if err != nil {
1267				return false, fmt.Errorf("nativemirror: apply completion %s: %w", id, err)
1268			}
1269			return tag.RowsAffected() > 0, nil
1270		}
1271		tag, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx,
1272			`UPDATE native_mirrors
1273			 SET status = $2, applied_position = GREATEST(applied_position, $3)
1274			 WHERE id = $1 AND `+completionEligible+`
1275			   AND (status <> 'ready' OR applied_position < $3)`,
1276			id, status, sourcePosition)
1277		if err != nil {
1278			return false, fmt.Errorf("nativemirror: apply completion %s: %w", id, err)
1279		}
1280		return tag.RowsAffected() > 0, nil
1281	}

656	// AdvanceStage is the fenced stage CAS: it moves id from → to only while
657	// the caller still holds the claim, the row is not marked for deletion, and
658	// it is not suspended. Returns false without error when the guard fails —
659	// the caller re-reads and decides (deletion intended → teardown leg;
660	// otherwise another executor won and this one walks away).

663	// transient failure that RecordRetry last recorded is resolved, so a healthy
664	// placement (e.g. one that reaches announced after an earlier retry) doesn't

1239	// prior sync failure but never resurrects a permanent creation failure;

content.content:
# Mirror-worker roles

Three workers consume `mirror_git_v1`, one per source kind, each bound to its own
durable:

| Workload | Source kind | Durable |
|---|---|---|
| mirror-worker-github | `github` | `mirror-git-v1-github-JUR-CLUSTER` |
| mirror-worker-native | `entiredb` | `mirror-git-v1-entiredb-JUR-CLUSTER` |
| mirror-worker-ns | `entiredb_ns` | `mirror-git-v1-entiredb_ns-JUR-CLUSTER` |

They share the pod template in `workload/`, which each role in `roles/` includes
with a `nameSuffix`. `workload/` is deliberately **not** a resource of `base/`:
including it directly is what used to materialise a fourth, suffix-less
`combined` worker consuming the wildcard subject. That role was retired in
ENT-2495 — it had been at zero replicas in every cell since the split, and
because it was defined by *negative* filters it silently absorbed the namespace
role's monitors (ENT-2344). Every unit is now defined by what it is.

All three roles share the `mirror-worker` identity and mTLS certificate; role
separation is capacity isolation, not an authorization boundary. ENT-2279 tracks
receiver-enforced privilege separation. Native configuration omits
`ENTIRE_CORE_INTERNAL_URL`. Role health hostnames append `-github`, `-native` or
`-ns`; routes permit only GET `/healthz` and `/readyz`, and the operator's POST
`/drain` is never routed through the gateway.

## Reconciliation states

Edit the **one** entry in `components` in the cell's overlay. Do not add multiple
states or remove the selector. Image promotion updates `images` and deployment
annotations in that same parent; it preserves the state.

| State | Effect |
|---|---|
| `active` | Normal autoscaling. KEDA owns replicas; rollouts use the default 600s progress deadline. |
| `frozen` | Current replicas held; KEDA and Deployment rollouts paused. |
| `paused` | Zero replicas; every scaler paused at zero. |

`active` restates the two fields `frozen` overrides rather than changing
anything, so a cell's state is always an explicit selection and the pair is
diffable.

Frozen Deployments set `progressDeadlineSeconds: 2147483647`, Kubernetes'
disabled-deadline sentinel. The deployed Flux kstatus checker otherwise waits for
`Progressing=True/NewReplicaSetAvailable` while Kubernetes reports
`Progressing=Unknown/DeploymentPaused` during the intentional pause. Disabling
the deadline only when frozen lets Flux keep assessing generation, replica counts
and pending termination.

[KEDA's `paused` annotation](https://keda.sh/docs/2.20/concepts/scaling-deployments/)
holds the current count; `paused-replicas` explicitly requests zero. Deployment
`spec.paused` prevents image/config promotions from replacing pods while an
operator drains them. A crashed or evicted pod can still be replaced: freeze is
not a guarantee of stable membership. Verify pod UIDs and restart counts again
after all drain requests; any change invalidates the drain inventory. A
successful Flux health check does not prove stable pod membership or a completed
drain.

An active Deployment deliberately omits `spec.replicas`, leaving scaling to KEDA.

## Draining a worker

Needed before deliberately removing pods — a node drain, a freeze, or any
operator action that should not abandon work in flight.

SIGTERM already settles: the worker closes fetch admission and waits up to
`ENTIRE_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (5m) for the in-flight sync before
exiting, which is why `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is 360 and must stay above
that budget. For an explicit, confirmable drain of a specific pod:

```
kubectl --context "$context" -n mirror-worker port-forward "pod/$pod" 18080:8080
curl --fail --show-error --max-time "$drain_timeout_seconds" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18080/drain
```

# Mirror-worker roles

Three workers consume `mirror_git_v1`, one per source kind, each bound to its own
durable:

| Workload | Source kind | Durable |
|---|---|---|
| mirror-worker-github | `github` | `mirror-git-v1-github-JUR-CLUSTER` |
| mirror-worker-native | `entiredb` | `mirror-git-v1-entiredb-JUR-CLUSTER` |
| mirror-worker-ns | `entiredb_ns` | `mirror-git-v1-entiredb_ns-JUR-CLUSTER` |

They share the pod template in `workload/`, which each role in `roles/` includes
with a `nameSuffix`. `workload/` is deliberately **not** a resource of `base/`:
including it directly is what used to materialise a fourth, suffix-less

| `frozen` | Current replicas held; KEDA and Deployment rollouts paused. |
| `paused` | Zero replicas; every scaler paused at zero. |
